definition: He put it (a thing, S Mgh, Msb) beneath his A_iboT [or arm-pit ];
sourceDefinition: He put it (a thing, S Mgh, Msb) beneath his A_iboT [or arm-pit ]; (S, Msb, K;) or in his A_iboT . (Mgh.) ― -b2- Hence, (K,) taA^ab~aTa $ar~aA , the surname of Thábit the son of Jábir (S, K) ElFahmee: (S:) because they assert that the sword never quitted him: (S:) or because he put beneath his arm—pit a quiver of arrows, and took a bow, or put beneath his arm—pit a knife, and came to an assembly of Arabs, and smote some of them. (K.) It is invariable: but if you desire to express the dual or pl., you say, *awaA taA^ab~aTa $ar~FA and *awuw taA^ab~aTa $ar~KA , or you say kilaAhumaA and kul~uhumo . (S.) It does not admit of the formation of a dim., nor is it abridged: (S, K:) but some of the Arabs used to say taA^ab~aTu [so written with refa], using a single word, accord. to Sb, as is said in the L. (TA.) Its rel. n. is ↓ taA^ab~aTiY~N . (S, K.) ― -b3- [Hence also] tA^b~T fulaAnN fulaAnFA (assumed tropical:) Such a one placed such a one under his protection. (TA.) ― -b4- tA^b~T also signifies He put his ridaA=' , (S,) or garment, (Mgh, K,) under his right arm, and then threw [a portion of] it over his left shoulder, (S, Mgh, K,) in prayer, or in A_iHoraAm ; (Mgh;) as also AiDoTabaEa . (S.) [See also tawa$~aHa .]

definition: [The armpit; ] the inner side of the shoulderjoint: (ISd, K:) or the part beneath the janaAH [which signifies the arm, upper arm, armpit, and wing, &c.]: (S, Msb:) also written ↓ A_ibiTN ; (Msb, K;)...
sourceDefinition: [The armpit; ] the inner side of the shoulderjoint: (ISd, K:) or the part beneath the janaAH [which signifies the arm, upper arm, armpit, and wing, &c.]: (S, Msb:) also written ↓ A_ibiTN ; (Msb, K;) which is said to be a dial. var. by some of the moderns; but this is strange, on account of what is said respecting A_ibilN ; (Msb;) for Sb says that there are only two substs. of the measure fiEilN , which are A_ibilN and HibirN ; and one epithet, namely bilizN : other instances have been mentioned, but their transmission from Sb is not established: (Msb. in art. Abl :) it is also said that there is no other word like A_ibilN ; but this means, in its original form, and does not deny that there are words like it by the insertion of a second vowel like the first, such as this and many other words: (TA:) [see also A_ibidN :] it is fem.; (Mgh;) or masc. and fem.; (S, Msb;) sometimes the latter; (Lh, K;) but the making it mase. is more approved: (TA:) Fr cites, from certain of the Arabs, the phrase, (S,) farafaEa Als~awoTa Hat~aY baraqato A_iboTuhu [ And he raised the whip so that his armpit shone ]: (S, Msb:) the pl. is A=baATN . (S, Msb, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] Daraba A=baATa AlA^umuwri wamagaAbinahaA (tropical:) [ He hit the secret and occult particulars of the affairs ]. (A, TA [followed by the words wa A@$otaq~a DamaAy^irahaA wabawaATinahaA , a pleonastic addition, merely explaining what goes before.]) ― -b3- And Daraba A=baATa AlmafaAzapi (tropical:) [ He traversed the recesses of the desert ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And A_iboTu jabalK (assumed tropical:) The foot, or bottom, or lowest part, ( safaHo ,) of a mountain. (TA.) ― -b5- And A_iboTu ramolK (assumed tropical:) The place where the main body of sand ends: (S:) or what is thin, of sand: (K:) or the lowest part of an oblong tract of sand collected together and elevated, where the main body thereof ends, and it becomes thin. (TA.) ― -b6- And A_ibETu Al$~imaAli (assumed tropical:) Evil fortune; ill luck. (TA.)

definition: The sword is beneath my A^iboT [or armpit ]: and Als~ayofu EiTaA fiY wa A_ibaATiY I put, or place, the sword upon my side, and beneath my A_iboT .
sourceDefinition: The sword is beneath my A^iboT [or armpit ]: and Als~ayofu EiTaA fiY wa A_ibaATiY I put, or place, the sword upon my side, and beneath my A_iboT . (TA.) And jaEalotuhu I put it (namely the sword, TA) next my A_iboT (K, TA.) The Hudhalee, (S, TA,) El-Mutanakhkhil, describing water to which he came to drink, (TA,) says, (S, TA,) accord. to the Deewán, but some ascribe the words to Taäbbata—Sharrà, (TA,) $aribotu bij~amihi waSadarotu Eanohu wa A^aboyaDu SaArimN *akarN A_ibaATiY meaning [ I drank of the main body thereof, and returned from it, and a sharp steel—edged sword was ] beneath my A_iboT : (S, TA:) or, accord. to one relation, the poet said, biA^aboyaDa SaArimK *akarK : and accord. to another, wa EaDobN SaArimN : Skr says that the last word of the verse is a contraction of A=baATiY : and Ibn-Es-Seeráfee, that it is originally ↓ A_ibaATiY~N ; and if so, it is an epithet. (TA.)

definition: , originally waHadN , the w being changed into A^ , (Msb,) One;
sourceDefinition: , originally waHadN , the w being changed into A^ , (Msb,) One; the first of the numbers; (S;) syn. [in many cases] with waAHidN ; (S, Msb, K;) with which it is interchangeable in two cases, to be explained below: (Msb:) pl. A=HaAdN and A^NHodaAnN (K) and A^aHaduwna , which last occurs in a phrase hereafter to be mentioned; (TA;) or it has no pl. in this sense; (Msb, K, * TA;) and as to A=HaAdN , it may be pl. of waAHidN , [and originally A^awoHaAdN ,] like A^a$ohaAdN as pl. of $aAhidN , (Th, Msb,) a pl. of pauc. (Msb.) The fem. is ↓ A_iHodaY only; and this is only used in particular cases, to be shown below: (Msb:) most agree that the Y in this word is the characteristic of the fem. gender: but some say that it is to render it quasi-coordinate to the quadriliteral-radical class: [this, however, is inconsistent with its pronunciation, which is invariably A_iHodaY , not A_iHod~aY :] (TA:) its pl. is A_iHadN , as though the sing. were A_iHodapN , like as is said of *ikarN as pl. of *ikoraY : one of the expositors of the Tes-heel writes it A^uHadN , with damm and then fet-h; but a pl. of this measure is not applicable to a sing. of the measure fiEolaY , with kesr. (MF.) The dim. of A^aHadN is ↓ A^uHayodN ; and that of A_iHodaY is ↓ A^uHayodaY . (L in art. wHd .) ― -b2- It is interchangeable with waAHidN in two cases: first, when it is used as an epithet applied to God: (Msb:) for AlA^aHadu , as an epithet, is applied to God alone, (Msb, K,) and signifies The One; the Sole; He who has ever been one and alone: or the Indivisible: or He who has no second [ to share ] in his lordship, nor in his essence, nor in his attributes: (TA:) you say, huwa AlwaAHidu and huwa AlA^aHadu : and in like manner, A^aHadN , without the article, is used as an epithet specially in relation to God, and is interchangeable in this case [but not in other cases] with waAHidN : therefore you do not say rajulN A^aHadN nor dirohamN A^aHadN and the like [but rajulN waAHdN and dirhamN waAHidN &c.] (Msb.) [See also waAHidN , in art. wHd .] In the phrase in the Kur [cxii. 1], qulo huwa All~`hu A^aHadN [ Say, He is God, One God], A^aHadN is a substitute for All~`hu ; for an indeterminate noun is sometimes a substitute for a determinate noun, as in another passage in the Kur, xcvi. 15 and 16. (S.) Secondly, it is interchangeable with waAHidN in certain nouns of number: (Msb:) you say A^aHada Ea$ara [masc.] and A_iHodaY Ea$orapa [fem.] (S) [meaning Eleven: and in these two cases you may not substitute waAHidN and waAHidapN for A^aHadN and A_iHodaY : but] in A^aHadNwEa$oruwna [ One and twenty, and the like,] A^aHadN is interchangeable with waAHidN . (Msb.) Ks says, When you prefix the article Al to a number, prefix it to every number; therefore you should say, maA faEalati AlA^aHada AlEa$ara AlA^alofa Ald~irohama [ What did the eleven thousand dirhems? ]: but the Basrees prefix it to the first only, and say, mA fElt AlA^aHada Ea$ara A^alofa dirohamK . (S.) ― -b3- In [most] cases differing from these two, there is a difference in usage between A^aHadN and waAHidN : the former is used in affirmative phrases as a prefixed noun only, governing the noun which follows it in the gen. case; [as in exs. which will be found below;] and is used absolutely in negative phrases; [as will also be seen in exs. below;] whereas waAHidN is used in affirmative phrases as a prefixed noun and otherwise: the fem. A_iHodaY , also, is only used as a prefixed noun, except in numbers (Msb) [and in one other instance, which see below]. Using A^aHadN and its fem. in affirmative phrases as prefixed nouns, you say, qaAma A^aHadu Alv~alaAvapi [ One of the three stood ]; and qaAlato A_iHodaA humaA [ One of them two (females) said ]; and xu*o A_iHodaY Alv~alaAvapi [ Take thou one of the three ]. (TA.) The phrase A_iHodaY banaAti TabaqK means A calamity: (K:) or, as some say, (TA, but in the K “ and, ”) a serpent; (K, TA;) so called because it twists itself round so as to become like a Tabaq . (TA.) And the phrase A_iHodaY AlA_iHadi , (L, K, TA,) in which the latter word has kesr to the A_ and fet-h to the H , and is pl. of the former, also written AlA^uHadi , but this form is disapproved by MF, as has been shown above, (TA, [in several copies of the K incorrectly written AlA^aHadi ,]) [lit. means One of the ones; and] is applied to a great, or mighty, event; (L, K, TA;) one that is difficult, distressing, grievous, or terrible. (L, TA.) You say, A^ataY biA_iHodaY AlA_iHadi [the last of which words is here again written in several copies of the K AlA^aHadi ] He brought to pass a grievous, and great, or mighty, event, (K, TA,) when you desire to express the greatness and terribleness of an event. (TA.) You also say, fulaAnu A^aHadu AlA^aHadiyna , and waAHidu AlA^aHadiyna , (K, TA,) the latter in one copy of the K written waAHidu AlwaAHidiyna , in which the latter word is pl. of the former, (TA,) and waAHidu AlA=HaAdi , and A_iHodaY AlA_iHadi , (K, TA,) like a phrase before mentioned, only the former is applied to a calamity, and this to an intelligent being, and written in the two manners before mentioned, the difference being only in application, (TA, [in several copies of the K here again written A_iHodaY AlA^aHadi , and in the CK AaHadiY~u AlAaHadi ,]) and A_iHodaY AlA^aHadiyna , (Et-Tes-heel,) and A_iHodaY AlA=HaAdi , (TA,) which are expressions of the utmost praise, (IAar, A Heyth, K,) [lit. Such a man is one of the ones; meaning] such a one is unique among the uniques; (TA;) one who has no equal; unequalled; incomparable. (IAar, Tes-heel.) It seems that the form of pl. used in the phrase A^aHadu AlA^aHadiyna is used only as applied to rational beings; but it is said in the Expositions of the Tes-heel that this phrase signifies One of the calamities; the form of the rational pl. being given to nouns significant of things deemed great, mighty, or grievous. definition: , originally wirovN , (T, S,) Inheritance;
sourceDefinition: , originally wirovN , (T, S,) Inheritance; or a person's obtaining possession of property left to him by one who has died. (MF.) ― -b2- An inheritance, or a heritage; what is inherited. (S, A, K.) ― -b3- An old condition, case, or state of things, which the last has inherited from the first. (S, A, K.) So in the phrase, huwa EalaY A_irovK mino ka*aA [ He is conforming, in respect of such a thing, with an old state of things, or an old usage, which he has inherited from his ancestors ]. (S.) And in the following ex., from a trad., A_in~akumo EalaY A_irovK mino A_irovi A^abiykumo A_iboraAhiyma [ Verily ye are conforming with an old state of things, or an old usage, which ye have inherited from your father Abraham ], the meaning is, that his religion was their heritage. (T, * TA.) [See also wirovN .] ― -b4- A remainder, or what remains, (M, L, K,) of a thing, (K,) or of the original of a thing: (M, L:) pl. A_iraAvN . (L.) ― -b5- And [hence, app.,] Ashes. (M, K.) ― -b6- Also Origin, race, or stock. (S, M, A, K.) You say, huwa fiY A_irovi SidoqK He is of an excellent origin, race, or stock. (S.) And A_in~ahu lafiY A_irovi majodK [ Verily he is of a glorious origin, race, or stock ]; as also A_irofi majodK , by a change of letters. (Yaa- koob, M.) Accord. to IAar, A_irovN relates to Hasab [or grounds of pretension to respect or honour, on account of one's ancestors' or one's own deeds or qualities, &c.]; and wirovN , to property, or wealth. (M.) [See art. wrv .]

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. , (T, S, M, Msb,) and , (so in the M accord. to the TT,) inf. n. A^amalN , (T, S, M, &c.,) this being the inf. n. accord. to IJ, [as distinguished from A^amolN and A_imolN ,] (M,) He hoped it; or hoped for it; syn. rajaAhu ; (S, * M, * [see A^amalN below,] K;) meaning, what was good for him; (S;) as also ↓ A^malhu , (T, * M, K,) inf. n. taA^mylN : (S, T:) or he expected it; [or had a distant, or remote, expectation of it; for] it is mostly used in relation to that of which the occurrence, or coming to pass, is deemed remote; as in the saying of Zuheyr, A^arojuw waA=mulu A^ano tadonuw mawad~atuhaA [ I hope, and have a distant expectation, that her love may approach ]: he who has determined upon a journey to a distant town or country says, A^amalotu AlwuSuwla [ I have formed an expectation, or a distant expectation, of arriving ]; but he does not say, TamiEotu until he has become near thereto; for TamaEN relates only to that of which the occurrence, or coming to pass, is [deemed] near: and Alr~ajaA='u is between AlA^amalu and AlT~amaEu ; for it is sometimes attended with fear that the thing expected may not come to pass, wherefore it is used in the sense of fear; and when the fear is strong, [lest the thing expected should not come to pass, it denotes distant expectation, and thus] it is used in the sense of AlA^amalu ; whence the usage in the verse of Zuheyr; but otherwise it is used in the sense of AlT~amaEu : (Msb:) or AlrjA' signifies the expectation of benefit, or advantage, from some preceding cause or means: so says El-Harállee: or it is properly syn. with AlA^amalu ; and in common conventional language, means the clinging of the heart to the coming to pass of a future desired event: so says Ibn-El-Kemál: or, accord. to Er-Rághib, an opinion requiring the coming to pass of an event in which will be a cause of happiness: (TA:) and ↓ A^m~lhu , inf. n. taA^omiylN , signifies he expected it much; and is more commonly used than the form without teshdeed. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K, &c.,) [in some copies of the K written bax~a , which is wrong, for it is] like balo , (A,) [i. e.] like qado , (TA,) [perhaps, as I have suggested above, from the sound made by a hecamel in a state of excitement,] a word used on the occasion of praising; (S, A;) on praising one from whom has proceeded a good and wonderful action; (Har p. 142;) on approving a thing; (T, S, Msb, K;) on being pleased with it, or having one's admiration excited by it; (A, K;) or on the occasion of glorying and of praising; (K;) in pronouncing a thing great in estimation, (IAmb,) or excellent; (AHeyth;) in deeming a thing great in estimation, (AHei,) or good; (Mgh;) or it means wonder, or admiration; (R;) and sometimes it is used [ironically] to denote disapproval; also, as an exhortation to gentleness with a thing, and to taking extraordinary pains; (TA;) and in a case of expertness, or skilfulness: (AHei:) it means niEoma Alr~ajulu and niEoma AlfiEolu [ Excellent, or most excellent, is the man! and, the deed! ]; (Har p. 142;) [or simply, excellent! or most excellent! how good! how goodly! well done! bravo! and the like;] or EaZuma AlA^amoru and faxuma [ great in estimation is the thing, or affair, or event, or case! ]: (K:) MF observes, [probably from finding bax~a in the place of baxo in his copy or copies of the K,] that this explanation is like an express assertion that it is a verb in the pret. tense, which requires consideration. (TA.) It is used alone; and in this case you say, baxo , (K,) and baxi , (Msb, K,) with kesr for its invariable termination, (Msb,) and baxK , and baxN ; (K, TA; [but in the CK, in the place of baxK and baxN , we find buxN ;]) without tesh-deed, (T, Msb,) in most cases; (Msb;) but also with teshdeed, (T, S, A,) like a noun; so that one says, baxK laka and bax~K [&c., meaning I say excel-lent! &c., to thee ]: (S:). and one repeats it, (S, A, K, &c.,) for the sake of emphasis; (S, A;) saying, baxo baxo , (IAmb, S, A, K, &c.,) with the x quiescent like the l in halo and balo , (IAmb,) and baxK baxK , (S, A, R, K,) pronounced in the latter manner, with tenween, when in connexion with a following word, [and in this case only, whereas it is pronounced in the former manner in any case,] (S, A,) and bax~K bax~K , (S, * A, * R, K,) and baxK baxo , (K,) and bax~i bax~i . (R.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. mubaAdarapN and bidaArN ; and ↓ Abtdrhu ; He hastened, or made haste, or strove to be first or beforehand, in doing [or attaining or obtaining ] it; (M, K, TA, TK;) namely, a thing: (M:) and gayoruhu A_ilayohi ↓ badara , (M, K,) aor. ; and bAdrhu Alyh ; (M;) He hastened with another, or vied or strove with him in hastening, to it [or to do or attain or obtain it ]: syn. EaAjalahu , (M, K, TA,) and A^asoraEa A_ilayohi . (TA.) bAdr [as well as ↓ badara and ↓ Abtdr ] denotes mutual effort only when it is immediately trans.: when it is trans. by means of A_ilaY [or bi (the former in the TA written by mistake ElY ], there is nothing to show that it denotes this. (MF.) [But it is often immediately trans. without its denoting such effort.] One says, bAdrhu He hastened to do it [&c., as explained above]; meaning, a thing that he desired, or wished for: (TA:) [and bAdrbihi signifies the same; or he hastened with it: and the former signifies also he betook himself early to him or it: ] and bAdr A_ilayohi he hastened to it; (S, A;) as also Alyh ↓ badara , (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. , (S,) inf. n. buduwrN : (S, Msb:) or, accord. to Zj, agreeably with its derivation, [see badorN ,] he employed the fulness of his power, or force, to hasten [ to it ]: (TA:) and AlA^amorN ↓ badarahu , and ↓ badara A_ilayohi , (aor. , inf. n. badorN , TA, [or buduwrN , as above,]) the thing, or event, came to him, or happened to him, hastily, quickly, or speedily; and, beforehand [or before he expected it ]; syn. Eajila , (M, K,) and sabaqa , (M,) or Aisotabaqa : (K:) [and minohu qawolN ↓ badara , and fiEolN , a saying, and an action, proceeded from him hastily, without premeditation: see baAdirapN .] It is said in a trad., baAdiruwA biAloA^aEomaAli haramFA [ Strive ye to be before decrepitude with good works; i. e., to perform them before decrepitude ]. (El-Jámi' es- Sagheer.) And in another, baAdiruwA AlS~uboHa biAlowitori [ Strive ye to be before daybreak with the prayers termed wtr ; i. e., to perform them before daybreak ]. (Idem.) And in another, baAdiruwA biSalAapi Almagoribi qabola TuluwEi Aln~ajomi [ Hasten ye with, or to perform, the prayer of sunset before the rising of the star ]. (Idem.) You say also, fulaAnN yubaAdiru fiY A^akoli maAli Alyatiymi [ Such a one hastens in consuming the property of the orphan before the latter is of full age]. (A.) And baAdara kibara Alyatiymi [ He hastened to be before the orphan's attaining to full age in expending his property ]; said of a guardian; i. q. fiy maAli Alyatiymi ↓ A^abodara : (K:) and thus, bidaArFAA^ano yakobaruwA , in the Kur [iv. 5], means hastening to be before their attaining to full age in expending their property. (Bd, * Jel.) And bAdrhu AlgaAyapa and A_ilaY AlgaAyapi [ He strove with him in hastening, or strove to get before him, to the goal ]. (A.) And AlgaAyapa ↓ Abtdr and A_ilaY AlgaAyapi [ He strove in hastening, or strove to get first, to the goal ]. (Ham p. 46.) And baAdara baEoDuhumo baEoDFA A_ilaY A^amorK , and A^amorFA ↓ AbtdrwA , and ↓ tbAdrwhu , They vied, or strove, one with another, in hastening to a thing, or an affair, trying which of them would be first. (T.)

definition: , (S, A, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K, &c.,) originally an inf. n., (Msb,) The full moon; (M, A, Msb, K;) as also ↓ baAdirN ; (L, K;) the moon in its fourteenth night: (S:) or the latter signifies [simply] the moon: (IAar, T:) the moon in its fourteenth night is called bdr because it hastens to rise before the sun sets; (S, M;) and to set before the sun rises: (TA:) or because of its fulness; (S, TA;) as being likened to a badorap : or, as Er-Rághib thinks to be most probable, it is itself a primitive word: (TA:) pl. buduwrN . (M, A.) Hence, layolapu Albadori [ The night of the full moon; which is] the fourteenth night [ of the lunar month ]. (S.) ― -b2- (tropical:) A lord, master, or chief, (M, K,) of a people: so called as being likened to the full moon. (M.) ― -b3- Applied to a boy, (Zj, M, K,) (tropical:) Full of youthful vigour and of flesh: (Zj:) or full, or plump: (M:) or i. q. ↓ mubaAdirN [ precocious ]. (T, K.) [In this sense, an epithet; and so its fem. badorapN (q. v.), applied to an eye.] ― -b4- (tropical:) A cover; or a dish or plate; syn. TabaqN : (Ibn-Wahb, K:) because resembling the full moon, being round: so Az thinks. (TA.) ― -b5- See also badorapN , in two places.

definition: Hastiness of temper;
sourceDefinition: Hastiness of temper; passionateness: (S:) or a hasty saying, or action, that suddenly proceeds ( yaboduru , in the CK yaboduw ,) from one in anger: (M, A, * Mgh, * Msb, * K:) and a slip; a mistake; an error; (S, Msb;) on an occasion of one's being angry: (S:) or a bad, an abominable, or a foul, word or saying: and a quick fit of anger: (IAar, T:) pl. bawaAdiru , (S, A.) You say, A^axo$aY Ealayoka baAdiratahu I fear for thee his hastiness of temper, or passionateness: (S:) or what may hastily proceed from him in his anger. (A.) And minohu yawaAdiru gaDabK ↓ badarato Slips, mistakes, or errors, on an occasion of his being angry, hastily proceeded from him. (S.) And baAdirapu Al$~ar~i signifies What hastily, or suddenly, befalls one, of evil, or mischief. (M.) ― -b2- An intuitive knowledge, notion, or idea; or a faculty of judging rightly at the first of an unexpected occurrence; or a faculty of extemporizing; syn. badiyhahN . (S, K.) You say, fulaAnu Hasanu AlbaAdirapi Such a one has a good intuitive knowledge, &c. (TA.) ― -b3- The point of a sword. (M, K.) ― -b4- The extremity of an arrow, next the head. (A.) ― -b5- The head of a plant; (M;) the first part thereof from which the earth cleaves asunder. (M, K. *) ― -b6- The first that appears of the [plant called] Hin~aA=' . (M.) ― -b7- The leaves of the [herb called ] Huw~aA='ap . (K.) ― -b8- The best, and freshest in growth, of the [plant called ] waros . (M, K. *) ― -b9- Also, (M, K,) or bawaAdiru , (S, A,) which is the pl., (K,) of a man &c., (S, M,) The portion of flesh, (S, M, K,) or the portions thereof, (A,) between the shoulder-joint and the neck, (S, M, K,) or between the necks and the shoulderjoints: (A:) or the former, (K,) or its dual, (M,) of a man, the two portions of flesh that are above the rugavaAwaAni and below the vanoduwap : (M, K:) or the dual, [relating to a camel, signifies] the two sides of the kirokirap [or callous lump on the breast ]: or two veins on either side thereof. (M.) ― -b10- bawaAdiru Alxayoli ↓ badarato The first, or fore parts, ( A^awaAy^il ,) of the horses appeared [or suddenly came in view ]. (Msb.)

And baraqati Als~amaA='u , (S, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (Msb, TA,) inf. n. baraqaAnN (As, S, Msb, K) and baroqN (Msb, TA) and buruwqN , (K,) The sky lightened; (Msb, K;) as also ↓ Abrqt : (AO, AA, K:) or gleamed or shone [ with lightning ]: (S, K:) or lightened much before rain; as also ↓ Abrqt . (K.) ― -b3- And [hence] said of a man, (JK, Msb, K,) or raEada wabaraqa , (S,) (tropical:) He threatened; (JK, S, K;) or he threatened with evil; (Msb;) [or he threatened and menaced; ] or he frightened (S and K in art. rEd ) and threatened; (S in that art.;) and ↓ Abrq signifies the same; (JK, Msb, K;) and so A^aroEada wa A^aboraqa : (K:) or, accord. to As, ArEd and Abrq are not allowable. But baraqato , inf. n. baroqN , said of a woman, (K,) or raEadato wa baraqato , (S,) means (tropical:) She beautified (S and A in art. rEd , and K) and adorned herself, (S, K,) [as also ↓ tbr~qt , (occurring in the K in art. Alq , coupled with its syn. tazay~anat ,)] and showed, or presented, herself, (A in art. rEd , and TA,) liY to me: (A in art. rEd :) or she exhibited her beauty intentionally: (TA:) and ↓ br~qt means the same, (Lh, K,) inf. n. taboriyqN ; (TA;) and so ↓ Abrqt : (K:) you say, biwajohihaA wasaAy^iri jisomihaA ↓ Abrqt (tropical:) She beautified herself in her face and the rest of her person: (Lh, TA:) and Eano wajohihaA ↓ Abrqt (tropical:) She showed her face. (JK, Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b4- Also, said of a star, or an asterism, It rose. (Lh, K.) One says, laA A^afoEaluhu maA baraqa Aln~ajomu fiY Als~amaA='i I will not do it as long as the star, or asterism, [by which may be meant the asterism of the Pleiades, ] rises in the sky. (Lh, TA.) ― -b5- baraqa AlbaSaru , (S,) or baSaruhu , (K,) The eye or eyes, or his eye or eyes, glistened, (S, K,) being raised, or fixedly open: (S:) or became raised, or fixedly open: occurring in the Kur [lxxv. 7], accord. to one reading: (Fr, TA:) or the eye, or his eye, became open by reason of fright. (TA.) bariqa has a different meaning, which see below. (S.) ― -b6- baraqato , said of a she-camel, She put her tail between her thighs, making it to cleave to her belly, without being pregnant: (IAar, TA:) or she raised her tail, and feigned herself pregnant, not being so; as also ↓ Abrqt , (Lh, S, K,) and Abrqt bi*anbihaA : (TA:) or Abrqt signifies she smote with her tail at one time upon her vulva and another time upon her buttocks; and also, she feigned herself pregnant, not being so. (JK.) ― -b7- bariqa He feared, so that he was astonished or amazed or stupified, at seeing the gleam of lightning: (TA voce baHira :) or his (a man's) sight became confused in consequence of his looking at lightning. (Bd in lxxv. 7.) And hence, (Bd ibid.,) bariqa AlbaSaru , (S, Bd,) or baSaruhu , (K,) aor. ; (S, K;) and baraqa , aor. ; (K;) or the latter has [only] a meaning explained above; (S;) inf. n. baraqN , which is of the former verb; (S;) accord. to the K, baroqN ; but this is wrong; (TA;) and [of the latter verb,] buruwqN ; (Lh, K;) The eye or eyes, or his eye or eyes, became dazzled, so as not to close, or move, the lid, or lids: (S, K:) or became confused, so as not to see. (K.) bariqa baSaruhu signifies also His eye or eyes, or his sight, became weak: whence bariqato qadamaAhu His two feet became weak. (TA.) Also bariqa alone, (TA,) inf. n. baraqN , (Fr, K, TA,) He (a man, TA) was frightened; or he feared, or was afraid: (Fr, K, TA:) and he became confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course. (K.) ― -b8- bariqa said of a skin, aor. , (JK, K,) inf. n. baraqN , (JK,) so in the O, in which, as in the K, the part. n., being bariqN , indicates that the verb is like fariHa ; (TA;) and baraqa , (K,) so in the L, (TA,) aor. , (K,) inf. n. baroqN and buruwqN ; thus in the L, which indicates that the verb is like naSara ; (TA;) It became affected by the heat so that its butter melted and became decomposed, (As, JK, K,) and did not become compact. (S.) -A3- bariqati Alganamu , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. baraqN , (S,) The sheep, or goats, had a complaint in their bellies from eating the barowaq : (S, K:) and in like manner, AlA_ibilu the camels. (K.) ― -b3- And [hence] said of a man, (JK, Msb, K,) or raEada wabaraqa , (S,) (tropical:) He threatened; (JK, S, K;) or he threatened with evil; (Msb;) [or he threatened and menaced; ] or he frightened (S and K in art. rEd ) and threatened; (S in that art.;) and ↓ Abrq signifies the same; (JK, Msb, K;) and so A^aroEada wa A^aboraqa : (K:) or, accord. to As, ArEd and Abrq are not allowable. But baraqato , inf. n. baroqN , said of a woman, (K,) or raEadato wa baraqato , (S,) means (tropical:) She beautified (S and A in art. rEd , and K) and adorned herself, (S, K,) [as also ↓ tbr~qt , (occurring in the K in art. Alq , coupled with its syn. tazay~anat ,)] and showed, or presented, herself, (A in art. rEd , and TA,) liY to me: (A in art. rEd :) or she exhibited her beauty intentionally: (TA:) and ↓ br~qt means the same, (Lh, K,) inf. n. taboriyqN ; (TA;) and so ↓ Abrqt : (K:) you say, biwajohihaA wasaAy^iri jisomihaA ↓ Abrqt (tropical:) She beautified herself in her face and the rest of her person: (Lh, TA:) and Eano wajohihaA ↓ Abrqt (tropical:) She showed her face. (JK, Ibn-'Abbád, K.) ― -b4- Also, said of a star, or an asterism, It rose. (Lh, K.) One says, laA A^afoEaluhu maA baraqa Aln~ajomu fiY Als~amaA='i I will not do it as long as the star, or asterism, [by which may be meant the asterism of the Pleiades, ] rises in the sky. (Lh, TA.) ― -b5- baraqa AlbaSaru , (S,) or baSaruhu , (K,) The eye or eyes, or his eye or eyes, glistened, (S, K,) being raised, or fixedly open: (S:) or became raised, or fixedly open: occurring in the Kur [lxxv. 7], accord. to one reading: (Fr, TA:) or the eye, or his eye, became open by reason of fright. (TA.) bariqa has a different meaning, which see below. (S.) ― -b6- baraqato , said of a she-camel, She put her tail between her thighs, making it to cleave to her belly, without being pregnant: (IAar, TA:) or she raised her tail, and feigned herself pregnant, not being so; as also ↓ Abrqt , (Lh, S, K,) and Abrqt bi*anbihaA : (TA:) or Abrqt signifies she smote with her tail at one time upon her vulva and another time upon her buttocks; and also, she feigned herself pregnant, not being so. (JK.) ― -b7- bariqa He feared, so that he was astonished or amazed or stupified, at seeing the gleam of lightning: (TA voce baHira :) or his (a man's) sight became confused in consequence of his looking at lightning. (Bd in lxxv. 7.) Also bariqa alone, (TA,) inf. n. baraqN , (Fr, K, TA,) He (a man, TA) was frightened; or he feared, or was afraid: (Fr, K, TA:) and he became confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course. definition: A certain kind of plant (JK, S) which camels do not feed upon except in cases of necessity;
sourceDefinition: A certain kind of plant (JK, S) which camels do not feed upon except in cases of necessity; (JK;) a small, feeble tree, which, when the sky becomes clouded, grows green: (K:) n. un. witIh p : (S, K:) it was described by an Arab of the desert to AHn as follows: a feeble, juicy plant, having slender branches, at the heads of which are small envelopes ( qamaAEiylu SigaArN ) like chick-peas, in which is a kind of black grain: its feebleness is such that it withers on the spot when the sun becomes hot upon it: and nothing feeds upon it; but men, when they are afflicted with dearth, or drought, express from it a bitter juice, then work it together, or knead it, with habiyd [or colocynths, or the pulp, or seeds, thereof], or some other thing, and eat it; but it is not eaten alone, because it occasions excitement: it is one of the plants that are plentiful in time of drought and scarce in time of fruitfulness; when copious rain falls upon it, it dies; and when we see it to have become abundant, and coarse, or rough, we fear drought: accord. to another of the Arabs of the desert, the barowaqap is a bad kind of herb, or leguminous plant, that grows among the first of the herbs, or leguminous plants: it has a reed like the sbAT [so I render lhA qSbp mvl AlsbAT , but I thing that the right reading is, lahaA quDubN mivolu Als~iyaATi it has twigs like whips, agreeably with the description next preceding, in which it is said to have slender branches,] and a black fruit, or produce. (TA.) Hence, A^a$okaru mino barowaqapK [ More grateful than a barwakah ]; (S, K;) because it grows green when it sees the clouds, (S,) or by means of the least moisture falling from the sky: (TA:) a prove. (S.) And A^aDoEafu mino barowaqapK [ Weaker than a barwakah ]. (TA.)

definition: A rope ( Habol ) having two colours;
sourceDefinition: A rope ( Habol ) having two colours; (S, O;) twisted with a black strand and a white strand: (JK:) and in like manner, (JK,) a mountain ( jabal , JK, K) in which are two colours, (K, TA,) black and white: (TA:) and (so in the S , but in the K “ or,”) anything having blackness and whiteness together. (S, K.) You say tayosN A^aboraqN and EanozN baroqaA='u [ A black and white he-goat and she-goat ]: (S, K:) and $aApN baroqaA='u a ewe whose white wool is cleft, or divided, by black flocks [or streaks ]: (K:) A^aboraqu and baroqaA='u applied to sheep or goats are like A^abolaqu and baloqaA='u applied to beasts of the equine kind, and A^aboqaEu and baqoEaA='u to dogs. (Lh, TA.) ― -b2- baroqaA='u is also a name given to An eye; (S, M;) because it has blackness and whiteness mingled in it: (M, TA:) dual baroqaAwaAni . (TA.) And EayonN baroqaA='u signifies An eye black in the iris, with whiteness [of the rest] of the bulb. (TA.) ― -b3- rawoDapN baroqA='u A meadorc, or garden, in which are two colours. (TA.) ― -b4- See also buroqapN . in seven places. ― -b5- A^aboraqu also signifies A certain bird. (Tekmileh, K.) ― -b6- And [the pl.] buroqN is used as a name for The [ locusts, or crickets, termed ] janaAdib . (IB, TA.) -A2- Also A certain Persian medicine, good for the memory. (Sgh, K.)

sourceDefinition: a Persian word, (S, Msb,) arabicized, (S, Msb, K,) originally A=bo riyzo (CK [in a MS. copy of the K and in the TA, incorrectly, A=b riy ]) [ A ewer, such as is used for wine, and also such as is used for water to be poured on the hands; each having a long and slender spout, and a handle;] a well-known vessel; (TA;) a vessel having a spout (Mgh, and Bd and Jel in lvi. 18) and a handle: (Bd and Jel ibid:) accord. to Kr, a kuwz ; and so says AHn in one place; but in another he says that it is like a kwz : (TA:) [it is somewhat like a kwz with the addition of a spout: ] pl. definition: signifies The removing of that which restrains one from free action.
sourceDefinition: signifies The removing of that which restrains one from free action. (TA.) [And hence,] ― -b2- baEavahu , (S, A, &c.,) aor. , (A, K,) inf. n. baEavN (Mgh, L, Msb, TA) and baEavN , (L, TA,) He sent him; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) namely, a messenger; (Msb;) and, when said of God, an apostle; (A;) [and when said of a man, a letter, &c.;] as also ↓ AbtEvh : (S, A, Msb, K:) [or] the former is said of anything that goes, or is sent, by itself; and of anything that will not go, or be sent, by itself, as a letter, and a present, one says, baEava bihi : (Msb:) [thus,] baEavahu signifies he sent him, or it, alone, by himself, or by itself; and baEava bihi , he sent him, or it, by, or with, another, or others: (L:) but El-Fárábee says that the former of these two has another signification, which will be found below; and that the latter signifies he sent him, or it. (Msb.) Hence, Duriba Ealayohimu AlbaEovu The being sent to the war was appointed them and imposed upon them as an obligation. (Msb.) You say, baEavahu lika*aA [ He sent him for such a thing or purpose ]. (A, TA.) [And baEava A_ilayohi bika*aA He sent to him such a thing; lit., he sent to him a messenger with such a thing. ] And baEava Aljunoda A_ilaY Algazowi [ He sent the army to the war ]. (TA.) And baEava Ealayohimu AlbalaA='a [ He sent upon them trial, or affliction; ] he caused trial, or affliction, to befall them. (TA.) ― -b3- Also, (A, L, TA,) inf. baEovN (Mgh, L, TA) and baEavN (L) and taboEaAvN [an intensive form], (TA,) He roused him, excited him, or put him in motion or action; (A, L, Mgh, TA;) namely, anything; (TA;) [i. e. any person or animal; and particularly,] an animal lying down, or a person sitting. (L, TA.) You say, baEava Aln~aAqapa He roused, or put in motion or action, the she-camel; (S, Mgh, K, TA;) i. e., loosed the cord that bound her shank to her arm, and dismissed her; or he roused her, or made her to rise, she being lying down. (TA.) It is said in a trad. respecting 'Áïsheh, fabaEavonaA AlbaEiyra fA_i*aA AlEiqodu taHotahu [ And we made the camel to rise, and to, the necklace was beneath him ]. (TA.) You say also, baEavahu EalaY AlA^amori , (A,) or Al$~aYo'i , (L,) He roused him, excited him, or put him in motion or action, to do the affair, or thing: (A:) or he incited him, urged him, or instigated him, to do the thing. (L.) ― -b4- Also, accord. to El-Fárábee, (Msb,) or baEavahu mino manaAmihi , (S, A, K,) inf. n. baEavN and baEavN , (TA,) He roused him, or awoke him, from his sleep; (S, A, Msb, K;) as also ↓ AbtEvhu . (TA, from a trad.) ― -b5- baEovN (S, K, TA) and baEavN (TA) also signify The quickening, vivifying, or revivifying, of the dead; the raising of the dead to life; (S, K, * TA;) by God, (TA,) on the day called yawomu AlbaEovi (S, TA) the day [ of resurrection, ] when those who are in the graves shall be raised. (A, Mgh.) You say, baEava A@ll~`hu Alxaloqa , and AlmawotaY , God quickened, vivified, revivified, or raised to life, mankind, and the dead. (TA.) -A2- baEiva , aor. , (inf. n. baEavN , TK,) He (a man, TA) was sleepless, or wakeful. (K, * TA.) [See baEivN .]

definition: , applied to a man, Voracious;
sourceDefinition: , applied to a man, Voracious; a great eater; as also ↓ bulaEapN and ↓ mibolaEN (K) and ↓ bawolaEN : (IAar, K:) [↓ bal~aAEo signifies the same:] and ↓ hibolaEN , (S and K in art. hblE ,) in which the h is said by some to be augmentative, (TA,) and ↓ habal~aEN (Lth, K) and ↓ hibolaAEN , (IDrd, K,) also signify the same; (S in art. hblE ;) or voracious, or a great eater, who takes large mouthfuls, and is wide in the Hunojuwr [app. here meaning the fauces ]: (Lth, and K in art. mblE :) and ↓ bulaEapN , applied to a woman, one who swallows everything. (Fr.) ↓ yaA bal~aAEa AlA^ayori [app. meaning yaA maA^obuwnu ] is an expression of vituperation used by the people of Syria. (TA.) ― -b2- saEodu bulaEa , (Lth, S, K,) determinate, (Lth, K,) [the latter word imperfectly decl.,] One of the Mansions of the Moon; (S, K;) [namely, the Twenty-third; ] which rose [aurorally], (S, K,) as they assert, (S,) when God said, yaA A^aroDu A@bolEiY maA='aki [Kur xi. 46]; (S, K;) consisting of two stars near together; (S;) or two stars, straight ( musotawiyaAni ) in course, (IKt, K,) or near together and oblique; (TA;) one of them dim, and the other bright, and called ↓ baAliEN , as though it swallowed the former, (IKt, K, TA,) namely, the dim one, and took its light: (TA:) it rises [aurorally] in the last night but one [lit. one night remaining] of kaAnuwn AlA=xir [Jan., O. S.], and sets [aurorally] when one night has passed of A=b [Aug., O. S.]. (IKt, K.) (Marginal note in a copy of the S.)

sourceDefinition: , (T, S M, &c.,) aor. yabiytu and yabaAtu , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. bayotuwtapN (Lth, T, S A, Msb, K) and mabiytN (Msb, K) and mabaAtN (Msb) and bayotN and bayaAtN , (K,) has two meanings: in that which more commonly obtains, the action is restricted to the night: (Msb:) it is by night, or in night; not in sleep: (M:) you say, baAta yafoEalu ka*aA , meaning He did such a thing by night, or at night: (S, Msb, K:) [or he was in the night, or at night, or during the night, doing such a thing: and he passed, or spent, the night, or a night, or a part thereof, or, as will be seen below, he entered upon the night, doing such a thing: ] like as one says, Zal~a yafoEalu ka*aA as meaning “ he did such a thing by day, ” or “ at day-time: ” (S, Msb;*) IKoot and Es-Sarakustee and IKtt say that it has this meaning, and not “ he slept: ” (Msb:) [F adds,] wa layosa mina Aln~awomi , (K,) which is said to mean, “ and the action is not one of sleep; ” so that when one sleeps by night, or at night, it is not correct to say, baAta yanaAmu : or, accord. to some, “ its meaning is not that of sleeping; ” so that one may say, baAta zayodN naAy^imFA [ Zeyd was in the night, &c., or passed, or spent, the night, &c., sleeping ]: (MF:) [Fei says,] it is only when one remains awake in the night: and hence the saying in the Kur [xxv. 65], waA@l~a*iyna yabiytuwna lir~abihimo suj~adFA waqiyAmFA [ And those who pass the night prostrating themselves to their Lord and standing up in prayer]: (Msb:) Fr says that baAta Alr~ajulu means The man remained awake all the night, engaged in acts of obedience or of disobedience: (T, Msb:) [or it means the man entered upon the night; or he was in the night, or at night, or during the night, in any state, or engaged in any action; for] Zj says, (M,) baAta is said of any one whom the night has overtaken, (M, K, *) whether he have slept or not slept: (M:) and Lth says, Albayotuwtapu signifies the entering upon the night: one says, bit~u A^aSonaEu ka*aA wa ka*aA [ I entered upon the night doing such and such things ]: and he adds, (T,) he who says baAta as meaning he slept commits an error; for you say, bit~u A^uraAEiY Aln~ujuwma [ I entered upon, or passed, the night ] looking at the stars: and how can he be sleeping who is looking at them? (T, Msb:) but Mullà 'Abd-El-Hakeem, in his Commentaries on the Mutowwal, says that baAta sometimes means he remained, continued, stayed, or dwelt, and he alighted and abode, by night, or at night, whether he slept or not: (MF:) and Ibn-Keysán says that it may be used in the same manner as naAma [ he slept ]; and also, [as will be explained below,] in the same manner as kaAna . (TA.) You say, baAta bayotuwtapF SaAliHapF (T) or Tay~ibapF (A) [ He passed, or entered upon, the night, or a night, in a good manner ]. And bit~u Alqawoma and bit~u bihimo and bit~u Einodahumo [ I passed, or entered upon, the night, or a night, with, or at the abode of, the people, or company of men: the last of these phrases is the most common]. (A 'Obeyd, M, K.) ― -b2- Secondly, it is used in the sense of SaAra [ He became ]; (Msb;) or in the same manner as kaAna [ he was ]. (Ibn-Keysán, TA.) One says, baAta bimawoDiEi ka*aA He became [or was ] in such a place; whether in night-time or in day-time. (Msb.) And hence the saying of the lawyers, baAta Einoda A@moraA^atihi layolapF He became [or was ] with his wife one night; [which is the same as he passed a night &c.; though this, it will be observed, is not in this instance the signification of the verb alone;] whether sleeping or not. (Msb.) ― -b3- [Thus it is used both as a “ complete, ” i. e. an attributive, verb, and also as an “ incomplete, ” i. e. a non-attributive, verb.] ― -b4- baAta , aor. yabiytu , (T, A,) inf. n. bayotN , (T, M, K,) also signifies (tropical:) He married, or took a wife: (T, A:) [see bayotN below:] or (assumed tropical:) he gave in marriage; syn. of the inf. n. tazowiyjN . (Kr, M, K.)

definition: He constructed, or built, the bayot [i.
sourceDefinition: He constructed, or built, the bayot [i. e. tent, or house, &c.]. (M.) -A2- by~t AlA^amori , [inf. n. as below,] He did, or performed, the thing, or affair, by night, or at night: (M:) and he thought, or meditated, upon it, considering its end, or issue, or result, (Zj, T, S, M, A, Msb, K,) or entered into it, (Zj, T,) by night, or at night. (Zj, T, S, M, &c.) And one says, buy~ita bilayolK , (T, A,) meaning the same as dub~ira bilayoli [ It was thought, or meditated, upon, &c., by night, or at night ]: (T:) [for] buy~ita Al$~aYo'u also signifies [simply] the thing was thought upon, and considered as to its end, issue, or result; syn. qud~ira . (S.) Accord. to El-Marzookee, they say of a thing that is not done deliberately, and with good consideration of its issue or result, h`*aA A^amorN qud~ira bilayolK ; [in the text from which this is taken, without the syll. signs;] and hence the saying in the Kur [iv. 83], bay~ata TaAy^ifapN minohumo gayori A@l~a*iY taquwlu [ A part of them meditateth by night upon doing otherwise than that which thou sayest; as is indicated in the M, where this is cited; and in like manner, yubay~ituwna , in the continuation of the same passage of the Kur, is explained in the T as meaning yudab~iruwna , and yuqad~iruwna , (i. e. mina Als~uwo'i ,) layolFA ]: but Aboo-Hilál says that a thing is meditated upon in the night in order that one may apply himself to it with strong purpose, and not be diverted by other things, so that it may be done with more firmness; and he cites the same passage of the Kur. (Ham p. 130.) And hence, in the Kur [iv. 108], A_i*o yubay~ituwna maA laA yaroDaY mina Alqawoli When they meditate, &c., (S, M, Bd, Jel,) by night, (S, M,) [ what He will not approve, of speech, ] and prepare it [ in their minds ] ( yuzaw~iruwnahu [see art. zwr ]). (Bd.) It is said in a trad., laA SiyaAma limano lamo yubay~iti AlS~iyaAma There is no fasting to him [meaning his fasting is null ] who does not purpose it from the night. (TA. [See another reading, voce bat~a .]) And you say, bay~ata Aln~iy~apa He decided upon the purpose, or intention, by night, or in night-time. (Msb.) And bay~ata raA^oyahu He thought upon his opinion, and concealed it, or conceived it, in his mind. (TA.) ― -b2- bay~atahumo , (inf. n. taboyiytN , (Msb, TA,) He came upon them, (Mgh, but the verb is there pl.,) or made a sudden attack upon them, and engaged with them in conflict, (Msb,) or made a great slaughter among them, or engaged with them in vehement conflict, (S, M, K,) namely, the enemy, (S, Mgh, K,) or a people, (M,) by night: (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K:) he came upon them (the sons of such a one) in the night, and made a sudden attack upon them, while they were heedless: (T:) he attacked them (the people of a house or place of abode) by night: he went to them (the enemy) in the night, without their knowledge, and took them by surprise. (TA.) ― -b3- kaAna laA yubay~itu maA lAFA walaA yuqay~iluhu He used not to retain property until night, nor to retain it until noon, when it came to him; but used to hasten the dividing of it. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b4- See also 4. -A3- by~t Aln~axola He trimmed, or pruned, the palm-trees, by cutting off the stumps of the branches, or by cutting off the straggling branches, not in the best part thereof. (K.) -A4- See also 5.

(TA.) ― -b3- kaAna laA yubay~itu maA lAFA walaA yuqay~iluhu He used not to retain property until night, nor to retain it until noon, when it came to him; but used to hasten the dividing of it. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b4- See also 4. -A3- by~t Aln~axola He trimmed, or pruned, the palm-trees, by cutting off the stumps of the branches, or by cutting off the straggling branches, not in the best part thereof. definition: [signifies A tent;
sourceDefinition: [signifies A tent; properly, having more than one pole; but often applied without this restriction: and also a house; a chamber; an apartment; a closet; and the like ]: a bayot is [ a tent ] of [ goats' ] hair ( $aEar ), (M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) or of wool: (Mgh:) a byt of hair [i. e. hair-cloth ] is that kind [ of tent ] which has more than one pole: the word is masc.: and applies to small and large: (M:) tents of goats' hair are peculiar to people of cold countries and of fertile regions, where the goats have abundant hair; for the goats of the Arabs of the desert have short hair, not long enough to be spun: (T in art. bnY :) a xibaA=' is a small byt of wool or of hair: a byt is what is larger than a xbA=' : next is the miZal~ap , which is larger than the byt ; but the term byt is also applied to a mZl~p when it is large and muraw~aq [i. e. furnished with a riwaAq , q. v.]: (T:) Ibn-El-Kelbee says that the Arabs have six kinds of byt ; namely, a qub~ap , which is of skins, or tanned hides; a miZal~ap , of hair; a xibaA=' , of wool; a bijaAd , of soft hair ( wabar ); a xayomap , of trees; an A^uqonap , of stone; and a sawoT , of hair; or this is the smallest of them: El-Baghdádee says that the xbA' is a byt made of soft hair ( wabar ), or of wool, or of hair [commonly so called] ( $aEar ), upon two poles, or three; and that a byt is [ a tent ] upon six poles, or more, to the number of nine: in the Towsheeh it is said that the term xbA' is applied to a byt of any kind: (TA:) a byt is also [ a structure ] of clay, or tough or cohesive clay or earth; (A, K;) [and of baked bricks; and of stone; ] the name being likewise applied to a structure of a kind other than the structures which are called A^axobiyap [or tents ]; (M;) signifying a habitation [ of any kind; an abode; a dwelling ]: (Msb:) a man's house; syn. daArN : (T:) [and particularly a chamber; i. e.] a single roofed structure (Mgh, Kull) having a place of entrance; manozilN being applied to what comprises more than one [such] byt , and a roofed SaHon [or vacant part, and a kitchen, inhabited by a man with his family]; and daArN , that which comprises more than one [such] byt and more than one [such] manozil and a [court, or] SaHon without a roof: (Kull:) the pl. is buyuwtN , (S, M, K, &c.,) also pronounced biyuwtN , (TA,) and A^aboyaAtN , (S, M, K,) the latter a pl. of pauc.; (TA;) and pl. pl. buyuwtaAtN (M, Mgh, K) and A^abaAyiytu (Sb, S, M, K) and A^aboyaAwaAtN , (Fr, M, K,) which last is extr.: (M:) the dim. is ↓ buyayotN , also pronounced ↓ biyayotN ; (S, K;) and the vulgar say, buwayotN , (S,) which is not allowable. (K.) You say, huwa jaAriY bayota bayota , (T, S, M,) He is my neighbour [ tent to tent, or house to house, i. e.,] by contiguity [ of our habitations ]: byt byt being made indecl. with fet-h for the termination because they are two nouns made one: (S:) Sb says that some of the Arabs make them [thus] indecl., like xamosapa Ea$ara , and some make the former a prefixed noun governing the latter in the gen. case, [saying bayota bayotK ,] except when used as a denotative of state: (M:) one says also, bayotFA libayotK , and bayotN libayotK ; (Fr, T;) which last, or bayotN A_ilaY bayotK , is the original form. (Har p. 353.) banaY fulaAnN EalaY A@moraA^atihi [lit. Such a one constructed a tent over his wife, ] means such a one had his wife conducted to him on the occasion of his marriage, and brought her, or had her brought, into a pitched tent, having conveyed thither the utensils and furniture and other things that they required. (T.) And A^aholu bayotu Aln~abiY~i [ The people of the house of the Prophet, ] means the Prophet's wives and his daughter and 'Alee: and so A^ahola A@lobayoti [i. e. yaxuS~u A^ahola Albayoti He means particularly, or peculiarly, the people of the house ], in the Kur xxxiii. 33: banuw and maEo$ar and A^ahol and A=l , as prefixed nouns, being, as Sb says, the nouns most frequently occurring in the accus. case [for the reason indicated above, or, as the Arabian grammarians express it,] EalaY AlAixotiSaASi . (M.) ― -b2- It also signifies A [ pavilion, palace, or mansion, such as is called ] qaSor : (T, K:) whence the saying of Gabriel, ba$~iro xadiyjapa bibayotK mino qaSabK , i. e. [ Rejoice thou Khadeejeh by the announcement of ] a pavilion ( qSr ) of hollow pearls, (T, TA,) or of emerald. (TA. [See also art. qSb .]) buyuwtFA gayora masokuwnapK [ Uninhabited houses ], in the Kur xxiv. 29, means buildings for the reception of travellers, or for merchants and their goods, and the shops of the merchants and places in which things are sold, the entering of which is allowed by their owners: or ruins which a man enters for the purpose of easing nature. (M.) And the buyuwt which God has permitted to be raised, mentioned in the same chapter, verse 36, are Mosques, or places of worship: or, accord. to El-Hasan, Jerusalem ( bayotu Almaqodisi ); the pl. being applied to it as a mark of honour. (Zj, M.) Albayotu [ The House ] applies particularly to (tropical:) the Kaabeh [ of Mekkeh ]; (K;) as also bayotu A@ll~`hi [ the House of God ]; (AAF, M;) and Albayotu AlHaraAmu [ the Sacred House ]; (T;) and Albayotu AlEatiyqu [ the Ancient House ]; (S and K &c. in art. Etq ;) and accord. to some, Albayotu AlmaEomuwru , q. v. (Bd in lii. 4.) [ bayotu AlmaAli signifies The treasury of the state. And bayotu AlmaA='i is a euphemism for The privy; because water is put there for the purpose of ablution: also called bayotu AlfaraAgi , &c.] ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) The ark of Noah: so in the Kur lxxi. last verse. (T.) ― -b4- (tropical:) A grave; (M, IAth, K;) app. by way of comparison. (M.) So in a trad. of Aboo-Dharr: kayofa taSonaEu A_i*aA maAta Aln~aAsu Hat~aY yakuwnu Albayotu biAlwaSiyfi , meaning How will thou do when men shall die so that the grave shall be sold for the [ servant- ] boy? (IAth.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) The habitation of the surofap , which it constructs in a beautiful manner, (A'Obeyd, M,) of fragments of sticks; (Yaakoob, M;) and of the SayodanaAniY~ , which it makes in the interior of the earth, and covers over: (A'Obeyd, M:) and (assumed tropical:) the burrow, or hole, of the Dab~ &c.: and (assumed tropical:) the web of the spider: all, app., as being likened to the bayot of a man. (M.) ― -b6- (tropical:) A man's household. (S, K, TA.) ― -b7- (tropical:) The wife (As, IAar, T, M, A) of a man. (M, A.) So in the saying, A^akibarN gay~araniY A^mo bayotu [ Hath old age altered me, or a wife? ]: (As, T:) or here it means a household. (S.) ― -b8- The nobility of the Arabs; (T, Msb, K; *) as when one says, bayotu tamiymK fiY baniY HanoZalapa [ The nobility of Temeem is in the sons of Handhaleh ]: (T, Msb: *) or the family that comprises the nobility of a tribe; as A=lu HiSonK of the fazaAriy~uwn , and A=lu Aljud~ayoni of the $ayobaAniy~uwn , and A=lu Eabodi AlmadaAni of the HaAriviy~uwn ; which three were asserted by Ibn-El-Kelbee to be the highest of the families thus called of the Arabs: (M:) [see a verse of El-Lahabee cited voce A^axoDaru :] pl. buyuwtN and buyuwtaAtN , (T, M,) the latter being pl. of the former. (T.) You say, huwa mino A^aholi AlbuyuwtaAti He is of the people of nobility: and mino bayotK kariymK [ of a generous, or noble, house, or family ]. (A.) [See also banaY .] ― -b9- A noble person: (M, Mgh, K:) pl. buyuwtN and buyuwtaAtN . (Mgh.) You say, fulaAnN bayotu qawomihi Such a one is the noble person of his people. (Abu-l-'Omeythil El-Aarabee, M.) ― -b10- (tropical:) The [ furniture termed ] faro$ , (A, Mgh, K,) or mataAE , (TA,) of a tent or house, (Mgh, K,) or that is sufficient for a tent or house. (A.) You say, tazaw~ajotu fulaAnapa EalaY bayotK (tropical:) I married, or took as a wife, such a woman for [ my giving ] furniture sufficient for a tent or house, (A,) or furniture of a house or tent. (Mgh.) [See 1, last sentence.] ― -b11- A bayot of poetry, (T, S, M, Msb,) or of the poet, (K,) is (tropical:) [ A verse; i. e.] what consists of certain known divisions [or feet ] called A^ajozaA='u Alt~afoEiyli ; being termed byt metaphorically, because of the conjoining of its component parts, one to another, in a particular manner, like as those of a tent are conjoined in its construction; (Msb;) because it consists of words collected together in a regular manner, and so resembles a tent, which is composed of a saqof and kifaA=' and riwaAq and Eumud : (T:) it is derived from the same word signifying a xibaA=' [or tent], and applies to the small and the great, as the rajaz and the Tawiyl ; and is [said to be] thus called because it comprises words like as the tent comprises its inhabitants; wherefore its component parts are termed A^asobaAb and A^awotaAd , as being likened to the AsbAb and AwtAd of tents: (M:) pl. A^aboyaAtN and buyuwtN , (M, A, Msb,) the latter mentioned by Sb and IJ, (M,) [but rare,] and [pl. pl.] A^abaAyiytu : (A:) Abu-l-Hasan says that if the byt of poetry be likened to the byt which is a tent or other kind of structure, there is no reason why it should not have the same pl. forms as the latter has. (L.) By the following words of a poet, wabayotK EalaY Zahori AlmaTiY~i banayotuhu biA^asomara ma$oquwqi AlxayaA$iymi yaroEufu [ Many a byt upon the back of the camel have I constructed with a lawny thing slit in the nose and bleeding ], is meant, many a byt of poetry have I written with the reed-pen. (S.) [ Albayota , written after a quotation of a part of a verse of poetry, means AiqoraA^i Albayota Read thou the verse. ] bayotu AlqaSiydapi [ The chief verse of the poem ] is a phrase employed when a person composes a poem in praise of any one from whom he would obtain some object of desire and want, being applied to that verse of the poem in which the author's want is mentioned: and is a proverbial expression relating to that which is extraordinary and strange, and used in denoting the superiority of a part of a thing over the whole of it [regarded as a whole]: [hence,] one says, fulaAnN A^aw~alu Aljariydapi wabayotu AlqaSiydapi (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one is the first of the detachment of horsemen, and the chief verse of the poem ]. (Har p. 441.)

And bayotu AlmaA='i is a euphemism for The privy; because water is put there for the purpose of ablution: also called bayotu AlfaraAgi , &c.] ― -b3- Also (assumed tropical:) The ark of Noah: so in the Kur lxxi. last verse. (T.) ― -b4- (tropical:) A grave; (M, IAth, K;) app. by way of comparison. (M.) So in a trad. of Aboo-Dharr: kayofa taSonaEu A_i*aA maAta Aln~aAsu Hat~aY yakuwnu Albayotu biAlwaSiyfi , meaning How will thou do when men shall die so that the grave shall be sold for the [ servant- ] boy? (IAth.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) The habitation of the surofap , which it constructs in a beautiful manner, (A'Obeyd, M,) of fragments of sticks; (Yaakoob, M;) and of the SayodanaAniY~ , which it makes in the interior of the earth, and covers over: (A'Obeyd, M:) and (assumed tropical:) the burrow, or hole, of the Dab~ &c.: and (assumed tropical:) the web of the spider: all, app., as being likened to the bayot of a man. (M.) ― -b6- (tropical:) A man's household. (S, K, TA.) ― -b7- (tropical:) The wife (As, IAar, T, M, A) of a man. (M, A.) So in the saying, A^akibarN gay~araniY A^mo bayotu [ Hath old age altered me, or a wife? ]: (As, T:) or here it means a household. (S.) ― -b8- The nobility of the Arabs; (T, Msb, K; *) as when one says, bayotu tamiymK fiY baniY HanoZalapa [ The nobility of Temeem is in the sons of Handhaleh ]: (T, Msb: *) or the family that comprises the nobility of a tribe; as A=lu HiSonK of the fazaAriy~uwn , and A=lu Aljud~ayoni of the $ayobaAniy~uwn , and A=lu Eabodi AlmadaAni of the HaAriviy~uwn ; which three were asserted by Ibn-El-Kelbee to be the highest of the families thus called of the Arabs: (M:) [see a verse of El-Lahabee cited voce A^axoDaru :] pl. buyuwtN and buyuwtaAtN , (T, M,) the latter being pl. of the former. (Abu-l-'Omeythil El-Aarabee, M.) ― -b10- (tropical:) The [ furniture termed ] faro$ , (A, Mgh, K,) or mataAE , (TA,) of a tent or house, (Mgh, K,) or that is sufficient for a tent or house. (A.) You say, tazaw~ajotu fulaAnapa EalaY bayotK (tropical:) I married, or took as a wife, such a woman for [ my giving ] furniture sufficient for a tent or house, (A,) or furniture of a house or tent. (Mgh.) [See 1, last sentence.] ― -b11- A bayot of poetry, (T, S, M, Msb,) or of the poet, (K,) is (tropical:) [ A verse; i. e.] what consists of certain known divisions [or feet ] called A^ajozaA='u Alt~afoEiyli ; being termed byt metaphorically, because of the conjoining of its component parts, one to another, in a particular manner, like as those of a tent are conjoined in its construction; (Msb;) because it consists of words collected together in a regular manner, and so resembles a tent, which is composed of a saqof and kifaA=' and riwaAq and Eumud : (T:) it is derived from the same word signifying a xibaA=' [or tent], and applies to the small and the great, as the rajaz and the Tawiyl ; and is [said to be] thus called because it comprises words like as the tent comprises its inhabitants; wherefore its component parts are termed A^asobaAb and A^awotaAd , as being likened to the AsbAb and AwtAd of tents: (M:) pl. sourceDefinition: That has remained throughout a night [ and so become stale; stale from being a night old ]; as also ↓ baAy^itN : both, in this sense, [but the latter more usually,] applied to bread. definition: , an arabicized word, (S, Msb, K,) from the Greek, (Msb, K,) [i.
sourceDefinition: , an arabicized word, (S, Msb, K,) from the Greek, (Msb, K,) [i. e. from θηριακὰ ,] or originally Persian, (S, O,) also written and pronounced diroyaAqN , (JK, Msb,) and TiroyaAqN ; (Msb;) or, as some say, from Alr~iyqu , because containing the spittle of serpents, and, if so, it is Arabic [in origin]: (Msb:) [ Theriac; also called treacle; ] an antidote for poisons; (S, O;) a certain compound medicine, (K,) comprising many ingredients, at most ninety or ninety-six, and at least sixty-four, (TA,) sometimes including the flesh of vipers, (K, TA,) and that of asses, which cause it to be prohibited and impure, or, as some say, it is prohibited without restriction: (TA:) it is a remedy against the bite or sting of rapacious venomous reptiles and the like, and poisonous potions: (K: [I omit some unprofitable and absurd particulars respecting the compounds thus termed, in the K and other lexicons &c.:]) pl. taraAyiyqu . (K in art. frq .) The best kind is called Alt~iroyaAqu AlfaAruwqu , (K in art. frq ,) vulgarly tiroyaAqN faAruwqiY~N . (TA in that art.) [A principal ingredient of this kind is the best sort of Jews-pitch, i. e. asphaltum, also called mumia, and in Arabic muwmiyaA :) (see De Sacy's “ Rel. de l'Égypte par Abdallatif, ” ” p. 274:) and this mumia, by itself, is called Alt~iroyaAqu Alt~urokiY~u .] ― -b2- [It is sometimes applied to Treacle, as meaning the sirop that drains from sugar. ] It is also said to be applied to the faAdozahor [or Bezoar-stone ], likewise termed masuwsN . (TA in art. ms .) ― -b3- Also, and ↓ tiroyaAqapN , (assumed tropical:) Wine; (S, O, K;) because it dispels anxiety; (S;) or because it is a remedy for anxieties; (O;) wherefore it is also termed SaAbuwnu Alhumuwmi . definition: He fatigued, tired, wearied, or jaded, another;
sourceDefinition: He fatigued, tired, wearied, or jaded, another; (S, Msb, K;) and himself, in a work that he imposed upon himself, or in which he laboured; and his travelling-camels, by urging them quickly, or by hard journeying. (TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) He broke a bone again after it had been set, or consolidated: or he caused a bone to have a defect in it, after it had been set, so that there remained in it a constant swelling, or resulted a lameness: AtEb AlEaZoma signifying A^aEonatahu baEoda Aljabori : (so in the CK:) or A^aEotabahu bEd Aljbr . (So in MS. copies of the K and in the TA. [In the latter, in art. Etb , this reading is confirmed; but a remark below, voce mutoEabN , rather favours the former reading, that of the CK.]) ― -b3- (tropical:) He filled a vessel; (A, K;) as, for instance, a drinking-cup, or bowl. (A.) -A2- AtEb Alqawomu The people's cattle became fatigued, tired, wearied, or jaded. (K.)

sourceDefinition: , a coll. gen. n.; (S, A;) masc. in one dial. and fem. in another [like other nouns of the same class]; (Msb;) Dates, or the fruit of the palmtree: (M:) or dried dates, like zabiybN as applied to grapes, by general consent of the lexicologists: (Mgh, Msb:) the dates are left upon the palmtree, after they have become ripe, until they are dry, or nearly so, when they are cut, and left in the sun to dry thoroughly; and sometimes, as AHát says, the fruit of the palm-tree is cut when full-grown but unripe, to lighten the tree, or from fear of theft, and left until it becomes tamor : (Msb:) the n. un. is with p : and the pl. of tamorN is tumuwrN and tumoraAnN , (T, S, M, Msb, K,) meaning sorts or varieties [ of tamor ]; for a coll. gen. n. has not a pl. in the proper sense: (S:) and in like manner the dual tamoraAni means two sorts [ of tamor ]: (Sb cited in the M in art. bsr :) the pl. of tamorapN is tamaraAtN . (S, K.) [See also busorN .] Hence the prov., A^aEoTi A^axaAka tamorapF faA_ino A^abaY fajamorapF [ Give thou thy brother a dried date; and if he refuse it, a live coal ]. (A, TA.) And Alt~amoru biAls~awiyqi [ Dried dates with meal of parched barley or wheat ] is another prov., used in allusion to requital. (Lh.) And one says, wajada Einodahu tamorapa AlguraAbi , meaning (tropical:) He found with him, or at his abode, what he approved. (A.) And nafosuhu tamorapN bika*aA (tropical:) His mind is pleased, or agreeably affected, with, or by, such a thing; or consents to such a thing. (A, K. * [Accord. to the TA, it is here like fariHapN ; but this seems to be true as to the meaning; not as to the form of the word. See also art. vmr , voce vamirN .]) And daEoniY A_in~a nafosiY gayoru tamorapK (tropical:) [ Leave thou me, or let me alone: verily my mind is not pleased, or happy ]. (A.) ― -b2- tamorN hinodiY~N [The fruit of the tamarindtree; thus called in the present day;] i. q. HumarN and HawomarN . (K in art. Hmr .)

sourceDefinition: , ('Eyn, T, M, K,) like EuniYa , (K,) and vay^iba , (IKoot, L, and so in a copy of the A,) inf. n. vaA^obN , (K,) or vaA^abN , (M,) He became relaxed and sluggish; said of a man: (A:) or he became affected with sluggishness and languor; (M;) as also ↓ tvA='b : (M, A:) or he became affected with sluggishness and languor like the languor of drowsiness; as also ↓ tvA='b and ↓ tvA^~b ; (K;) which last is approved by IDrd and Thábit Es-Sara- kustee, who disallow ↓ tvA='b , though this is the form commonly known and approved, and is the most chaste form: (TA:) or he became affected with languor like the heaviness of drowsiness, in consequence of something that he had eaten or drunk, without becoming insensible; (T;) as also ↓ tvA='b : (L:) or ↓ this last signifies he yawned, or opened his mouth, (Mgh, Msb,) by reason, (Mgh,) or on the occasion, (Msb,) of languor (Mgh, Msb,) like the heaviness of drowsiness; (Mgh;) or he yawned, or opened his mouth, and stretched himself, on being affected by sluggishness or drowsiness or anxiety; (MF, TA, on the authority of IDrst;) or he yawned, or opened his mouth, and emitted wind from his stomach, by reason of some affection thereof: (TA on the authority of EtTedmuree:) Alt~avaAw^ubu is from Alv~uw^abaA='u ; (AZ, T, S, Mgh;) and is on the occasion of one's stretching himself, and being languid: (Lth, T:) one should not say tavaAwaba ; (AZ, T, S, O, Mgh;) [for] this is vulgar. (Msb.) Hence, A^aHadukumo faloyugaT~i ↓ A_i*aA tavaA^a'aba faAhu [ When any one of you yawns, he should cover his mouth with the back of his left hand; for it is believed that the devil leaps into the uncovered yawning mouth]. definition: The qimaE [or base ] of a date: (S, K:) or the qimaE of a full-grown unripe date;
sourceDefinition: The qimaE [or base ] of a date: (S, K:) or the qimaE of a full-grown unripe date; i. e., the round portion of its covering, surrounding the stalk, and adhering to the upper part of the date: (Mgh:) or the part (El-'Adebbes, A-'Obeyd, S, K) of the date (El-'Adebbes, A'Obeyd, S) to which the qmE adheres: (El-'Adebbes, A'Obeyd, S, K:) or, accord. to Lth, the connecting medium ( ElAqp ) between the stone of the date and the qmE ; and AZ says the like: (TA: [see farDN as signifying a sort of dates of 'Omán:]) or a raceme of which the dates have been eaten, or of which all the dates have been stripped off except one or two or three: (ISh, TA:) pl. vafaAriyqu ; (S, K;) explained by Ks as meaning the A^aqomaAE of fullgrown unripe dates. (S.) tuforuwqN is a dial. var. thereof. (TA in art. tfrq .) The pl. also signifies The bases ( A^aqomaAE ) of grapes: (JK:) or the vuforuwq of a grape is what adheres to the raceme; and a closed perforation therein. (Mgh.) ― -b2- [Hence,] maA lahu vuforuwqN (assumed tropical:) He possesses not anything. (JK, Ibn-'Abbád, K.)

definition: A place where one remains, stays, dwells, or abides;
sourceDefinition: A place where one remains, stays, dwells, or abides; (T;) a place of alighting or abode, an abode, or a dwelling, (T, M, Mgh, Msb,) of a man: (T:) pl. mavaAwK (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K.) Hence, A^abuw AlmavowaY The master (M, K) of the house or tent, (M,) or of the place where one alights or abides, or of the abode or dwelling. (K.) And A^um~u AlmavowaY The mistress of the house or tent. (M.) And A^abuw mavowaY Alr~ajuli The master of the place of alighting, or of the abode, of the man: (S:) the host who entertains the man; to whom he betakes himself for lodging, and at whose abode he stays: (Har p. 595:) and the guest whom the man entertains. (M, K. * [See also vawiY~N .]) And A^um~u mavowaY Alr~ajuli The mistress of the place of alighting, or of the abode, of the man: (S:) the mistress of the man's place of alighting, or abode, in which he passes the night; occurring in this sense in a trad., not meaning his wife. (TA.) ― -b2- It is also an inf. n. of vawaY . (T, M.)

definition: A man having the eyeball, or globe of the eye, prominent and apparent;
sourceDefinition: A man having the eyeball, or globe of the eye, prominent and apparent; (TA;) or large and prominent; (S, TA;) as also ↓ jaHoZamN , in which the m is augmentative. (S, TA.) And jaAHZu AlEayonayoni A man whose blacks of his eyes are prominent. (TA.) You say also, fulaAnN jaAHiZN A_ilaY~a biEayonihi , and ↓ mujaH~iZN , meaning Such a one is looking at me intently. (T, TA in art. znr .) And juH~aZN and juHuZN , [which are pls. of jaAHiZN ,] applied to men, signify Raising the eyes, and looking fixedly; or stretching and raising the sight; or opening the eyes and not moving the eyelids. (L, TA.)

definition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. ja*obN ; (S, Msb;) as also jaba*ahu , (S, TA,) inf. n. jabo*N , of the dial. of Temeem, (TA,) or formed by transposition; (S, TA; [but see art. jb* ;]) and ↓ Ajt*bhu ; (S, A, K;) He drew it; dragged it; pulled it; tugged it; strained it; extended it by drawing, or pulling or tugging; stretched it; extended, lengthened, or protracted, it; (S, A, K;) namely, a thing; and sometimes relating to an ideal object. (TA.) ― -b2- ja*aba mina AlA_inaA='i , (S,) or ja*aba mina AlmaA='i , (K,) or ja*aba AlmaA='a , (A, Msb,) nafasFA , (S, A, Msb, K,) or nafasayoni , (S, A, Msb,) (tropical:) He drank (S, K) from the vessel, (S,) or of the water, (K,) by putting his mouth into it, [ a draught, or two draughts: ] (S, K:) or he conveyed [or drew up ] into the innermost parts of his nose [ a draught, or two draughts, of the water ]. (Msb.) And ja*abato labanahaA (tropical:) She (a camel) drank her milk when she was milked. (A. [But see what next follows: and see also 5.]) ― -b3- ja*abato , said of a she-camel, (S, K,) and of a she-ass also, aor. , inf. n. ji*aAbN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) She became scant of milk; (S, K;) she drew her milk ( ja*abato labanahaA ) from her udder so that it went away upwards. (TA.) ― -b4- ja*abahu , (K,) or ja*abahu Eano A^um~ihi , (S, A,) aor. , inf. n. ja*obN , (TA,) (tropical:) He weaned him; namely, a colt, (S, A, K,) and a young camel, and a lamb. (TA.) And one says of a mother, ja*abato waladahaA (tropical:) She weaned her young one: so accord. to Lh, who does not specify the kind. (ISd, TA.) And accord. to the T, ju*iba is said of a child, or of a lamb or kid, meaning (tropical:) He was weaned. (TA.) ― -b5- ja*abahu and ↓ jaA*abahu He transferred, or removed, it (a thing) from its place. (K.) ― -b6- ja*abatohu (tropical:) She repelled him, or rejected him; namely, a man who sought her in marriage; (T, A, TA;) as though from the saying jaA*abotuhu faja*abotuhu [which see below]; (T, TA;) [i. e.] as though she contended with him and overcame him, and thus he became separated from her; (T, A, TA;) as also jaba*atohu . (T, TA.) [Accord. to the TA, ↓ jaA*abatohu has the same meaning; but I think that this is a mistake of a copyist.] ― -b7- ja*aba fulaAnN Habola fulaAnihi (assumed tropical:) Such a one severed the bond of his union. (M, TA.) And ja*aba fulaAnN AlHabola bayonanaA (tropical:) Such a one severed the bond of union between us. (A, TA.) ― -b8- ja*aba Aln~axolapa , aor. , (AHn, K,) inf. n. ja*obN , (AHn, TA,) He cut off the ja*ab [q. v.] of the palm-tree, (AHn, K,) to eat it. (AHn, TA.) ― -b9- ja*aba AlEadowa (assumed tropical:) He ran quickly. (L in art. mEd .) See also 7. ― -b10- ja*ab Al$~ahoru , (S, A, K,) aor. , inf. n. ja*obN , (TA,) (tropical:) The greater part of the month ( EaAm~atuhu , S, A, K, i. e. A^akovaruhu , TA) passed. (S, A, K.) -A2- ja*abahu , aor. , He overcame him in AlmujaA*abap (K) [lit. drawing, dragging, pulling, &c.; (see 3;) but also] used figuratively [as meaning (tropical:) he overcame him in contention ]. (TA.) You say, ↓ jaA*abotuhu faja*abotuhu [ I contended with him in drawing, dragging, &c., and I overcame him therein: and also] (tropical:) I contended with him and I overcame him. (T, A, * TA.)

(S, K.) ― -b2- jarama Al$~aApa , (K,) or jarama Suwfa Al$~aApi , (S,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He shore, or sheared, or cut off the wool of, the sheep. (S, K, * TA.) And jaramotu minohu I took [or clipped somewhat ] from it; [namely, the wool;] like jalamotu . (S.) ― -b3- jarama Aln~axola , (S, Msb, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) inf. n. jaromN (K) and jaraAmN and jiraAmN , (S, * K,) He cut the palmtrees; (Msb;) [meaning] he cut off the fruit of the palm-trees; (S, K;) as also ↓ Ajtrmhu : (S:) and in like manner, jarama Alt~amora he cut off the dates. (TA.) You say, h`*aA zamanu AljaraAmi and AljiraAmi , (S,) i. e. [ This is ] the time of the cutting off of the fruit of the palm-trees. (TA.) ― -b4- And jarama Aln~axola , inf. n. jaromN , He computed by conjecture the quantity of fruit upon the palm-trees; (K;) and so ↓ Ajtrmhu : (Lh, K:) [like jazamahu and Ajtzmhu .] -A2- jarama , (S, K,) aor. , (S,) inf. n. jaromN , (TK,) also signifies He gained, acquired, or earned, [wealth, &c.,] (S, K,) liA^aholihi for his family; and so ↓ Ajtrm . (K.) And you say, xaraja yajorimu liA^aholihi and yajorimu A^aholahu , meaning He went forth seeking [sustenance], and practising skill, or artifice, for his family. (TA.) ― -b2- walaA yajoriman~akumo $anaA=nu qawomK , in the Kur [v. 3 and 11], is explained by some as meaning And let not a people's hatred by any means occasion you. or cause you: or it means let not a people's hatred by any means induce you, or incite you. (S, TA.) Some read ↓ lA yujoriman~akumo , with damm to the Y ; and Zj says that jaramotu and A^ajoramotu signify the same: but some say that the meaning is, let it not by any means lead you into crime, or sin; A^ajoramotuhu being like A=vamotuhu , I led him into sin, &c. (TA.) ― -b3- Fr says that the asserting jaramotu to mean Haqaqotu [or rather Huqiqotu , for this is evidently, I think, the right reading, though I find Haqaqotu in the TA as well as in a copy of the S, in another copy of which I find jaramato and Haq~aqato , suggesting that the right reading may perhaps be jaramato and Huq~ato ,] is nought: they who so explain it having been confused in their judgment by the saying of the poet Aboo-Asmà, (S, TA,) or, as some say, El-Howfazán, (TA,) or, accord. to some, 'Ateeyeh Ibn-'Ofeyf, (IB, TA,) walaqado TaEanotu A^abaA Euyayonapa TaEonapF jaramato fazaArapa baEodahaA A^ano yagoDabuwA in which they made fzArp to be in the nom. case, as though the meaning were Huq~a lahaA AlgaDabu [ it was right, or fit, or proper, for it, (the tribe of Fezárah,) to be angry; nearly agreeing with an explanation of jarama given by Golius as on the authority of Ibn-Maaroof, namely, “ meritus, dignus fuit ”]: but, he says, fzArp is in the accus. case; the meaning being, jaramatohumu AlT~aEonapu A^ano yagoDabuwA [which will be found explained, on the authority of IB, in what follows]: AO says that the meaning is, A^aHaq~ato Ealayohimu AlgaDaba , i. e., A^aHaq~ati AlT~aEonapu fazaArapa A^ano yagoDabuwA , and Haq~at also, [both having the same signification, i. e., the thrust required Fezá- rah to be angry, ] from laA jarama laA^afoEalan~a ka*aA meaning Haq~FA [ Verily I will do thus ]: (S, TA:) accord. to Fr, the meaning is, kasabato fazaArapa AlgaDaba Ealayoka , the right reading being, walaqado TaEanota , with fet-h to the t ; [so that the verse means And verily thou didst thrust Aboo-'Oyeyneh with a thrust of thy spear that occasioned, or caused, Fezárah, after it, to be angry against thee:] for he is addressing Kurz El-'Okeylee, bewailing his death; and Kurz had thrust Aboo-'Oyeyneh, who was Hisn Ibn-Hudheyfeh Ibn-Bedr El-Fezáree. (IB, TA.) ― -b4- And jarama , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , inf. n. jaromN , (Msb,) He committed a sin, a crime, a fault, an offence, or an act of disobedience; (S, Msb, K;) syn. A^a*onaba , (Msb, K,) and Aikotasaba AlA_ivoma ; (Msb;) [perhaps because he who does so brings upon himself the consequence thereof; as though originally jarama nafosahu Awlinafosihi A^avara juromK he drew upon himself the effect of a sin, &c.; (compare kasaba and Aikotasaba ;)] as also ↓ Ajrm , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_ijoraAmN ; (Msb;) and ↓ Ajtrm ; (S, K;) and ↓ tjr~m . (El-'Okberee, Har p. 207.) You say, jarama Ealayohimo jariymapF , and A_ilayohimo , (K,) and bihimo , used by a poet for Elyhm or Alyhm , (IAar, TA,) He committed against them a crime, or an offence for which he should be punished; as also ↓ Ajzm . definition: , (S, A, K,) like qaTaAmi , (K,) indecl.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, K,) like qaTaAmi , (K,) indecl., with kesr for its termination, because it deviates from its original form, which is jaAEirapN , and is of the fem. gender, and has the quality of an epithet in which that of a subst. is predominant, so that the thing to which it applies is known by it like as it is known by its proper name; and as it is prevented from being perfectly decl. by two causes, it must be indecl. by reason of three; as we also say with respect to HalaAqi , a proper name of death; (S;) The she-hyena; (S, A, K;) a name of that animal (S) because of the abundance of its dung; (S, A;) as also A^um~u jaEaAri , and ↓ jayoEarN , and ↓ A^um~u jaEowarK . (K.) Hence, A^aEoyavu mino jaEaAri [ More mischievous than the she-hyena ]: a prov. (A, TA.) And tiysiY jaEaAri (K) Be thou like the he-goat in stupidity, O she-hyena; a prov. applied to a stupid man: (A and TA in art. tys , q. v.:) or EiyviY jaEaAri [ Do mischief, O she-hyena ]; a prov. used in declaring a thing to be vain, or false. (K.) And ruwEiY jaEaAri waA@noZuriY A^ayona Almafori [for Almafir~u , Be afraid, O she-hyena, and look where is a place to which to flee ]: (K, * TA:) or ruwgiY [i. e. turn aside, this way and that ]: (S and TA in art. rwg :) a prov. applied to him who seeks to escape, and cannot: (TA:) or with reference to a coward, and his submissiveness. (K.) And quwmiY jaEaAri [ Rise, O she-hyena ]: said to a woman, in reviling her; likening her to a she-hyena. (ISk, TA.)
