sourceDefinition: , aor. yaTiyru , (S, Msb,) inf. n. TayaraAnN (S, A, Msb, K) and TayoruwrapN (Lh, S, K, &c.) and TayorN , (K,) He (a winged creature) moved in the air by means of his wings; flew; (A, K;) moved in the air as a beast does upon the ground. (Msb.) ― -b2- It is also said of other things than those which have wings; as in the saying of El- 'Amberee (Kureyt Ibn-Uneyf, Ham p. 3): TaAruwA A_ilayohi zaraAfaAtK wawuHodaAnaA [ They fly to it in companies and one by one ]; (TA;) i. e. they hasten to it: for Tirotu A_ilaY ka*aA means (assumed tropical:) I hastened to such a thing: and Tirotu bika*aA (assumed tropical:) I outstripped, or became foremost, with such a thing. (Ham p. 6.) And TAr EalaY matoni farasihi (tropical:) He fled upon the back of his horse. (TA, from a trad.) And TAr Alqawomu (assumed tropical:) The people took fright and ran away quickly. (Msb.) And TaAruwA siraAEFA (assumed tropical:) They went away quickly. (TA.) ― -b3- [One says also, TAr Euqoluhu (assumed tropical:) His reason fled. And TAr fuw^aAduhu (tropical:) His courage (lit. his heart ) fled away: see also 10: and see $aEaAEN . (Both are phrases of frequent occurrence.)] ― -b4- And TAr TaAy^ruhu : see TaAy^irN . ― -b5- [And see an ex. voce $iq~apN .] ― -b6- TAr qalobiY maTaArahu means (assumed tropical:) My heart inclined towards that which it loved, and clung to it. (TA, from a trad.) And TiyriY bihi , addressed to a woman, is expl. by IAar as meaning (assumed tropical:) Love thou, or become attached, to him. (TA.) ― -b7- TArt Eayonuhu (S and K in art. xlj ) (assumed tropical:) His eye throbbed. (PS and TK in that art.) ― -b8- TAr lahu SiytN fiY Aln~aAsi (tropical:) [ He became famous among the people; lit. means fame among the people became, or came to be, ( SaAra ,) his ]. (A.) [And in like manner one says,] TAr lahu mino naSiybihi ka*aA (tropical:) Such a thing became his, or came to him, of his lot, or portion; syn. SaAra , and HaSala . (Mgh.) And TAr lanaA (tropical:) It came to our lot, or portion. (TA.) And TAr likul~K minohumo sahomuhu (tropical:) The share of each came to him. (TA.) ― -b9- See also 6, in two places. -A2- TaAra bihi is also syn. with Tay~arahu , q. v. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence the metaphorical phrase TaArato bihaA AlEarabu expl. voce EarabapN .] ― -b3- TArt AlA_ibilu biA=*aAnihaA , (TA,) or biA^a*onaAbihaA , (O, TA,) thus [correctly] in the TS, (TA,) [like $aAlato biA^a*onaAbihaA ,] means (assumed tropical:) The she-camels conceived. (O, TA.)

definition: A flying thing [ whether bird or insect ]: (Msb, * TA:) pl.
sourceDefinition: A flying thing [ whether bird or insect ]: (Msb, * TA:) pl. ↓ TayorN , (S, Msb, K,) like as SaHobN is pl. of SaAHibN : (S, Msb:) or TayorN is originally an inf. n. of TaAra : or an epithet contracted from Tay~irN : (TA:) or a quasi-pl. n.; (Mgh, TA;) and this is the most correct opinion: (TA:) [but see, below, a reason for considering it originally an inf. n.:] and TaAy^irN may also be quasi-pl. n., like jaAmilN and baAqirN : (TA:) ↓ TayorN is also sometimes used as a sing.; (Ktr, AO, S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as in the Kur iii. 43 [and v. 110], accord. to one reading: (S:) but ISd says, I know not how this is, unless it be meant to be [originally] an inf. n.: (TA:) [for an inf. n. used as an epithet is employed as sing. and pl.:] or TaAy^irN , only, is used as a sing., (Th, IAmb, Msb,) by general consent; and AO once said so in common with others: (Th:) but ↓ TayorN has a collective, or pl., signification: (IAmb, Msb:) and is fem.: (Mgh:) or is more frequently fem. than masc.: (IAmb, Msb:) the pl. of TayorN is TuyuwrN [a pl. of mult.] and A^aToyaArN [a pl. of pauc.]: (S, Msb, K:) or TuyuwrN may be pl. of TaAy^irN , like as sujuwdN is pl. of saAjidN : (TA:) TaAy^irapN is seldom applied to the female. (IAmb, Msb.) ― -b2- [ AlT~aAy^ir is a name of (assumed tropical:) The constellation Cygnus; also called Ald~ajaAjapu .] ― -b3- huwa saAkinu AlT~aAy^iri means (tropical:) He is grave, staid, sedate, (K,) or motionless; so that if a bird alighted upon him, it would be still; for if a bird alight upon a man, and he move in the least, the bird flies away. (TA.) Of the same kind also is the saying, ruziqa fulaAnN sukuwna AlT~aAy^iri waxafoDa AljinaAHi (tropical:) [ Such a one was endowed, or has been endowed, with gravity and gentleness ]. (TA.) And Tuyuwruhumo sawaAkinu (tropical:) They are remaining fixed, settled, or at rest: and $aAlato naEaAmatuhumo signifies the contrary. (A, TA.) And ↓ kaA^an~a EalaY ruw^usihimu AlT~ayora (tropical:) [ As though birds were on their heads ] is said of a people, meaning them to be motionless by reason of reverence: (S, K:) it was said of the Companions of Mohammad, describing them as quiet and grave [in his presence], without levity: and the origin of the saying is this: that birds alight only upon a thing that is still and inanimate: (TA:) or that the crow alights upon the head of the camel, and picks from it the ticks, (S, K,) and the young ones thereof, (S,) and the camel does not move (S, K) his head, (S,) lest the crow should take fright and fly away. (S, K.) In like manner, waqaEa TaAy^iruhu means (tropical:) He became grave, or sedate. (Meyd.) And TaAy^iruhu ↓ TaAra (tropical:) He became light, or inconstant: (Meyd:) and he became angry; (O, K, TA;) like vaAra vaAy^iruhu and faAra faAy^iruhu : (TA:) or he hastened, and was light, or active, or agile. (Har p. 561.) ― -b4- And it is said in a trad., Alr~uw^oyaA EalaY rijoli TaAy^irK maA lamo tuEab~aro (O, TA) (assumed tropical:) A dream is unsettled as to its result, or final sequel, while it is not interpreted. (TA.) [The Arabs hold that the result of a dream is affected by its interpretation: wherefore it is added in this tradition, and said in others also, that the dreamer should not relate his dream, unless to a friend or to a person of understanding.] ― -b5- ↓ Eay~avato Tayoruhu see expl. in art. Eyv . ― -b6- TaAy^irN also signifies A thing from which one augurs either good or evil; an omen, a bodement, of good or of evil: (K:) and ↓ TiyarapN (S, K) and ↓ TiyrapN (K) and ↓ TiwarapN (IDrd, Sgh, K, TA [in the CK, in this art., erroneously, TuwrapN , but in art. Twr it is Tiwarap ,]) a thing from which one augurs evil; an evil omen or bodement; (S, K, &c.;) contr. of faA^olN : (TA:) and TaAy^irN signifies fortune, (A'Obeyd, K, TA,) whether good or evil: (TA:) and especially evil fortune; ill luck; as also ↓ TayorN and ↓ TiyarapN : for the Arabs used to augur evil from the croaking of the crow, and from birds going towards the left: [see 5:] (TA:) and ↓ TiyarapN is an inf. n. [or rather a quasi-inf. n.] of taTay~ara , [q. v.,] (IAth,) and signifies auguration of evil. (Msb.) The Arabs used to say, to a man or other thing from which they augured evil, (TA,) TaAy^iru A@ll~`hi laA TaAy^iruka , (ISk, S, IAmb,) and TAy^ra All~`h lA TAy^rak , meaning What God doth and decreeth, not what thou dost and causest to be feared: (IAmb:) accord. to ISk, one should not say A@ll~`hi ↓ Tayoru : (S:) but the Arabs are related to have said, also, laA Tayora A_il~aA Tayoru A@ll~`hi [ There is no evil fortune but that which is of God ]; like as one says, laA A^amora A_il~aA A^amoru A@ll~`hi . (As, S.) They also used to say, jaraY lahu AlT~aAy^iru biA^amori ka*aA [ Fortune brought to him such an event ]: and hence fortune, whether good or evil, is called TAy^r . (TA.) And it is said in the Kur [vii. 128], A_in~amaA TaAy^iruhumo Einoda A@ll~`hi , meaning Their evil fortune, which will overtake them, is only that which is threatened to befall them in the latter state, [ with God, ] and not that which befalls them in the present state of existence: (TA:) or the cause of their good and evil is only with God; i. e., it is his decree and will: or the cause of their evil fortune is only with God; i. e., it is their works, which are registered with Him. (Bd.) It is said in a trad., that Mohammad liked what is termed faA^ol , and disliked what is termed ↓ Tiyarap : (S:) and in another, that he denied there being any such thing as the latter. (TA.) -A2- Also The means of subsistence; syn. rizoqN . (K:) or misery: or happiness: every one of these three significations has been assigned to it in the Kur xvii. 14: in which, accord. to AM, it is meant that God has decreed to every man happiness or misery, according as He foresaw that he would be obedient or disobedient. (TA.) [See also what immediately follows.] -A3- Also The actions of a man which are [ as it were ] attached as a necklace to his neck. (S, Msb, K.) And this is [also said by some to be] its signification in the Kur xvii. 14. (Jel.) [The actions of a man are the cause of his happiness or misery.] -A4- AlT~aAy^iru signifies also The brain. (AAF, L, K.)

definition: (tropical:) Spreading;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) Spreading; applied to dust; as also ↓ Tay~aArN ; (TA;) and to hoariness; and to evil: (L:) rising and spreading; (K;) whereof the light spreads in the horizon; applied to the true dawn, which renders it unlawful to the faster to eat or drink or indulge in other carnal pleasure, and on the appearance of which the prayer of daybreak may be performed, and which is termed AlxiyoTu AlA^aboyaDu : that to which the epithet musotaTiyl is applied is [the false dawn,] that which is likened to the tail of the wolf ( *anabu Als~iroHaAni ), and is termed AlxiyoTu AlA^asowadu ; and this does not render anything unlawful to the faster. (TA.) ― -b2- Also A dog excited by lust; (Lth, O, K;) and so a camel; (K;) or the epithet applied in this sense to the latter is haAy^ijN . (Lth, O, TA.)

definition: A morsel of sawiyq [or meal of parched barley ];
sourceDefinition: A morsel of sawiyq [or meal of parched barley ]; (S, O;) i. q. HabakapN ; (S, K;) but this last word was not known to Az on any other authority than that of Lth. (TA in art. Hbk .) One says, maA *uqotu EabakapF walaA labakapF , meaning I tasted not a morsel of sawiyq nor a bit of variyd [or crumbled bread moistened with broth ]. (Lh, K, TA.) ― -b7- Eavara bihi : see 4. ― -b8- [Hence,] Eavara bihimo Alz~amaAnu (tropical:) Time, or fortune, destroyed them: (TA:) or caused them to be overcome. (O.)

definition: He caused him to stumble, or trip;
sourceDefinition: He caused him to stumble, or trip; or to fall upon his face; [or simply, to fall; ] as also ↓ Ev~rhu ; (K, TA;) [and so bihi ↓ Eavara ; (see 1, last sentence, and see also EaAvuwrN , first sentence;)] said of God. (TA.) IAar cites as an ex., faxarajotu A^uEovaru fiY maqaAdimi jub~atiY lawolaA AlHayaA='u A^aTarotuhu A_iHoDaAraA [ And I went forth, made to stumble, or trip, upon the fore parts of my jubbeh: but for the sense of shame, I had made it to fly, in running ]: accord. to one relation, however, the verb in question, in this verse, is A^aEovuru . (TA.) And AEvrhu A@ll~`hu is syn. with A^atoEasahu [of which see various explanations in art. tEs ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] AEvr bihi Einoda Als~uloTaAni , (K,) or Einodahu ↓ Ev~rhu , (A,) (tropical:) He impugned his character to the Sultán, (A, O, K,) and sought to make him fall into destruction by means of the latter. (A.) ― -b3- And AEvrhu Ealayohi (tropical:) [ He made him to stumble upon it, or to light on it by chance; or] he made him to get, or obtain, knowledge of it, or sight and knowledge of it; to become acquainted with it; to know it; or to see it; (S, A, O, Msb, K; *) accidentally, or without seeking. (B, TA.) Hence the phrase in the Kur [xviii. 20] A^aEovaronaA Ealayohimo ; (S, Ta;) in which gayorahumo , the objective complement, is suppressed. (TA.) And AEvrhu EalaY A^aSoHaAbihi (tropical:) He guided him, or showed him the way, to his companions. (A.) ― -b4- AEvr jad~ahu , and ↓ Ev~rhu , (assumed tropical:) He [i. e. God] made his fortune, or good fortune, to fall. (K. [See Eavara jad~uhu .]) -A2- See also 1, latter half.

definition: A stumble, or trip, (Msb, TA,) in walking, or going along: pl.
sourceDefinition: A stumble, or trip, (Msb, TA,) in walking, or going along: pl. EavaraAtN . (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence,] (tropical:) A slip, lapse, fault, wrong action, or mistake; (S, O, Msb, TA;) so called as being a fall into sin or crime. (Msb.) One says, A^aqaAla A@ll~`hu Eavorataka (tropical:) [ May God cancel thy slip, lapse, fault, &c.]. (A.) And it is said in a trad., laA Haliyma A_il~aA *uw EavorapK i. e. (tropical:) There is no one to be characterized as of a forbearing disposition except he be one who has committed a slip, and becomes admonished thereby, distinguishing the occasions of error so as to avoid them [and to make allowance for others who have done the like]. (TA.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) War, or fight, against unbelievers or others; because war, or fight, is an occasion of frequent stumbling, or tripping: so in a trad., in which it is said, laA tabodaA^ohumo biAlEavorapi (assumed tropical:) [ Begin not ye with them by war ]; meaning invite ye them first to El-Islám or to the payment of the poll-tax; and if they assent not, then have recourse to war. (TA.)

definition: A raceme of a palm-tree, or of dates;
sourceDefinition: A raceme of a palm-tree, or of dates; syn. Ei*oqN : or, when it has become dry and curved: (K:) or the base, or lower part, ( A^aSol , S, K, and also A and Mgh and Msb in art. Erj [because the n is therein regarded as augmentative],) of the Ei*oq (S, K) or kibaAsap [which signifies the same as Ei*oq ], (A, Mgh, Msb,) which curves, and from which the fruit-stalks are cut off, and which then remains upon the palm-tree, dry: (S:) or the Euwd [meaning main stem ] of the kibaAsap : (Th, K:) Az says, it is yellow and broad: [but it is the contrary of broad in comparison with its length:] and in the Kur xxxvi. 39, the moon when it has become slender [in appearance, towards the end of the lunar month,] is likened to the old Eurojuwn , in respect, as ISd says, of its slenderness and curvature: (TA:) [in the TA voce subaATapN , the pl. EaraAjiynu is strangely used as meaning the fruit-stalks of the raceme of a palmtree:] banaAtu EurojuwnK signifies the fruit-stalks of a raceme of dates: (T in art. bnY :) [it is said that] the n of EurojuwnN , though this word imports the meaning of AinoEiraAjN [or “ a state of bending ”], is shown to be radical by the word muEarojanN , occurring in a verse of Ru-beh, and also by the fact that there is no verb of the measure faEolana . (TA. [But Ea$orana and saboEana , though these are said to be post-classical, and, accord. to some, Ealowana , may be mentioned, and perhaps some other, as being of this measure.]) ― -b2- Also A certain plant, (K, TA,) white, accord. to Th, (TA,) like the fuTor [or toadstool ], resembling the fiqoE [ a white and soft sort of kamo' ], (K, TA,) which dries, having a round form: or a species of the kamoA^ap , of the measure of a span, or a little less than that; good, or pleasant, while fresh: (TA:) pl. EaraAjiynu . (K.)

definition: [ A species of mimosa;
sourceDefinition: [ A species of mimosa; called by Forskål mimosa örfota; (see his Flora Ægypt. Arab., pp. cxxiii. and 177;)] a sort of trees of the [ description termed ] EiDaAh , (S, O, K,) which exudes [ the gum called ] mugofuwr , and of which the fruit ( baramap ) is white and round: (S:) it has a gum of disagreeable odour ; and when bees eat it, somewhat of its odour is found in their honey: (TA:) AHn says that, accord. to Aboo-Ziyád, it is of the EDAh , and spreads upon the ground, not rising towards the sky, and has a broad leaf, and a sharp, curved thorn; it is of those trees of which the bark is stripped off and made into well-ropes; (O, TA;) and there comes forth from its fruit ( baram ) what is termed Eul~afapN , [i. e. a pod, ] resembling a bean, (O, * TA,) which is eaten by the camels and the sheep or goats: (O:) it is said by another, or others, that its fruit ( baramap ) is called fatolap , and is white, as though fringed with cotton; (O, TA;) like the button of the shirt, or somewhat larger: (O:) Aboo-Ziyád [further] says, (TA,) it is compact in its branches; has no wood that is useful like other wood; and has abundance of gum, which sometimes drops upon the ground until there are, beneath the trees, what resemble great mill-stones: Sh says that it is a short tree, the branches of which are near together, having many thorns; its height is like that of a camel lying down; it has a small, diminutive leaf; grows upon the mountains; and the camels eat it, particularly desiring the upper extremities of its branches: (O, TA:) [the word is a coll. gen. n.:] the n. un. is with A_ibilN EurofuTiy~apN . (O, K.)

definition: , (S, O, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, K,) aor. , (S,) inf. n. EarokN , (S, O,) He rubbed it, or rubbed and pressed it, or did so well; syn. dalakahu ; namely, a thing; (S, O;) such as a skin or hide, or a tanned skin or hide, and the like. (TA.) ― -b2- And [ He wore it away by scraping, &c.;] he scraped, rubbed, chafed, or fretted, it, until he erased, or effaced, it. (K.) ― -b3- Hence, Earaka bijanobihi maA kaAna mino SaAHibihi , aor. and inf. n. as above, meaning (assumed tropical:) [ He acted ] as though he scraped, &c., [ with his side, ] what had proceeded from his companion, until he erased, or effaced, it: (TA;) [like as a camel allays an itching by rubbing with his side the trunk of a tree: i. e. he bore, or endured, what proceeded from his companion: for] yaEoruku AlA^a*aY bijanobihi means yaHotamiluhu [i. e. (assumed tropical:) He bears, or endures, annoyance, or molestation; or forgives it, and feigns himself neglectful of it ]. (O and K in explanation of EurakapN .) ― -b4- And Earakotu Alqawoma fiY AlHarobi , inf. n. as above, (assumed tropical:) [ I fretted, or ground, or crushed, the party in the war, or battle. ] (S, O.) And Earakatohumu AlHarobu i. q. daArato Ealayohimo (tropical:) [i. e., lit., The war, or battle, revolved upon them like the mill or mill-stone; meaning fretted, or ground, or crushed, them ]. (TA.) Zuheyr says, fataEorukokumu Earoka Alr~aHaY bivifaAlihiA wataloqaHN ki$aAfFA vum~a tunotajN fatutoy^imi (O) meaning (tropical:) And it, i. e. war, will fret [or grind or crush ] you, as the mill with its skin put beneath it, upon which the flour falls, frets [or grinds ] the grain; and it, i. e. war, will conceive two years, one after the other; then bring forth, and give birth to twins: he makes war's destruction of them to be like the mill's grinding of the grain, and the various evils that are engendered from war to be like children. (EM pp. 123-4.) ― -b5- Earaka A^u*unahu , (MA,) inf. n. EarokN , (MA, KL,) He rubbed, or rubbed and pressed, [or generally, as now used, he wrung, or twisted, ] his ear. (MA, KL.) ― -b6- Earaka ZahorahaA , aor. and inf. n. as above, He felt her back, namely, that of a she-camel, &c., doing so much or often, to know her state of fatness: (TA:) and Earaka Als~anaAma He felt the hump, to know if there were in it fatness or not. (S, O, TA.) ― -b7- Earaka AlbaEiyur janobahu bimirofaqihi , (S, K, *) inf. n. as above, (TA,) The camel made an incision, or a cut, in his side with his elbow, (K, TA,) and rubbed it, or rubbed and pressed it, (TA,) so as to reach to the flesh, (K, TA,) cutting through the skin: (TA:) in which case the epithets ↓ EaArikN and ↓ EarakorakN are applied to the camel. (K.) [See also EarokN below, which indicates another meaning.] ― -b8- Earakahu (Lh, K, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (Lh, TA,) also signifies (assumed tropical:) He put upon him evil (Lh, K, TA) and misfortune: (K, TA: [the CK has Hamala Elyhi Al$~ar~u wAld~ahoru , meaning evil and misfortune assailed him, instead of Hamala Ealayhi Al$~ar~a waAld~ahora , as in other copies of the K and in the TA:]) and, as some say, Earakahu bi$ar~K signifies he did evil to him, or brought evil upon him, repeatedly. (TA.) ― -b9- Earaka Ald~ahoru fulaAnFA (tropical:) Time, or fortune, rendered such a one experienced; or trained, or disciplined, and reformed, or improved, him. (K, TA.) ― -b10- Earaka AlA_ibila fiY AlHamoDi He left the camels amid the plants termed HamoD , to obtain thereof what they wanted. (Lh, K.) ― -b11- Earakati AlmaA$iyapu Aln~abaAta The cattle ate the plants, or herbage. (K.) ― -b12- Earakato said of a woman, (S, O, K,) or of a girl, or young woman, (Lh, TA,) aor. , (S, O,) inf. n. EuruwkN (S, O, K) and EaraAkN (O, * K) and EarokN , (K,) She menstruated; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ AErkt . (K.) -A2- Earika , (K,) [aor. ,] inf. n. EarakN , (TA,) He was, or became, such as is termed EirikN [q. v.]; strong, or vehement, in striving, contending, or conflicting, (K, TA,) and in might, courage, valour, or prowess, (TA,) in war, or battle, (K, TA,) and in altercation. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: Fishermen; (AA, S, MA, O, K;) as also ↓ EarakapN ; (MA; [but this I do not find elsewhere;]) and EuruwkN : (O, K:) one of whom is called ↓ EarakiY~N , (AA, S, MA, O, K,) meaning a fisherman who holds in his hand an iron implement having five prongs: (MA:) EarakN and ↓ EarakiY~N being like EarabN and EarabiY~N : (AA, S, O:) [i. e. EarakiY~N is the n. un.:] accord. to the K, EarakN and EuruwkN are pls. of EarakiY~N ; but IAth says that EuruwkN is pl. of EarakN : (TA:) hence EarakN is used as meaning sailors, or mariners, (AA, S, O, K,) because they fish, not as being [properly] a name for them: (AA, S, O:) Zuheyr says, tago$aY AlHudaApu bihimo Hur~a Alkaviybi kamaA yugo$iY Als~afaAy^ina mawoja All~uj~api AlEaraku [ The camel-drivers cover with them the middle of the elevated expanse of sand like as the seamen cause the waves of the deep to cover the ships ]: but AO related this verse otherwise, saying mawoju , in the nom. case, and making AlEaraku to be an epithet applied to the mwj as signifying AlmutalaATim [as though the meaning were, like as the colliding waves of the deep cover the ships with their surf]. (S, O.) -A2- Also i. q. SawotN [ A sound, noise, voice, &c.]; and so ↓ EarikN . (S, O, K.) -A3- It is also the subst. denoted by the phrase Earaka AlA_ibila fiY AlHamoDi [q. v., app. as meaning The act of leaving camels amid the pasturage termed HamoD , to obtain thereof what they want; a meaning given in the O as an explanation of ↓ EarakorakN , which is perhaps in this instance a mistranscription]. (K.)

definition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. EaDobN , (S, A, O, &c.,) He cut, or cut off, him, or it. (S, A, * Mgh, * O, Msb, K.) maA lahu EaDabahu A@ll~`hu , meaning [ What aileth him? ] may God cut off (O, TA) his arm and his leg, or his hand and his foot, (O,) or his arms and his legs, or his hands and his feet, is a form of imprecation used by the Arabs. (TA.) And hence, (O,) one says, A_in~a AlHaAjapa layaEoDibuhaA TalabuhaA qabola waqotihaA (assumed tropical:) Verily the seeking of the object of want before its time assuredly cuts it off, or precludes it, and mars it: a prov. (O, TA.) And A_in~aka lataEoDibuniY Eano HaAjatiY (assumed tropical:) Verily thou cuttest me off from [ the attainment of ] the object of my want. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence] (assumed tropical:) He reviled him; (A, * K;) and (A) so EaDabahu bilisaAnihi . (S, A, O.) ― -b3- And He beat him, or struck him, (O, K,) with a staff, or stick. (O.) ― -b4- And He thrust him, or pierced him, (K,) with a spear. (TK.) [But in the O and TA, EaDabotuhu biAlr~umoHi is expl. by the words huwa A^ano ta$ogalahu Eanohu ; and the meaning app. is, I occupied him so as to divert him with the spear; though this meaning would be expressed more agreeably with usage by saying hw An y$glh Enh ; or rather hw An ta$ogalahu Eanoka , which, I think, is the right reading.] ― -b5- And It (disease, O) rendered him weak, or infirm: (S, O:) and (O) deprived him of the power of motion. (A, * O, K.) You say, EaDabatohu Alz~amaAnapu , aor. as above, (O, TA,) and so the inf. n., (TA,) meaning [ Disease of long continuance, or want of some one or more of the limbs, ] deprived him of the power of motion: and AHeyth says, it [in the O huwa (so that it does not refer to AlzmAnp ), and in the TA AlEDb ,] is Al$~alalu and Alxabolu and AlEaraju [ a state of privation of the power of motion, and unsoundness, and lameness; app. meaning that these are the effects denoted by the phrase EDbth AlzmAnp ]. (O, TA.) ― -b6- See also 4. -A2- EaDaba , (O, K,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (K,) signifies also He returned (O, K) Ealayohi [ against him ]. (O.) -A3- EaDiba , said of a ram, (K,) or EaDibat , said of a $aAp [i. e. sheep or goat, male or female], (S, O, Msb,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. EaDabN , (S, O, Msb,) He, or she, had the inner [ part of the ] horn broken: (S, O, Msb, K:) or had one of the horns broken. (S, O, Msb.) ― -b2- AlEaDabu is mostly used in relation to the horn: but sometimes, in relation to the ear: (A 'Obeyd, TA:) one says of a $Ap [expl. above], and of a she-camel, EaDibat , inf. n. EaDabN , meaning He, or she, had her ear slit, or had a slit ear: (Msb:) [or had half, or a third, of the ear cut off; for] accord. to IAar, AlEaDabu in relation to the ear is when half, or a third, thereof has gone. (O.) -A4- EaDuba , aor. , inf. n. EuDuwbapN (S, O, K) and EuDuwbN , (O, K,) said of a man's tongue, (tropical:) It was, or became, sharp in speech; (S, O, * K, TA;) being likened to a sharp sword. (O.)

(A.) ― -b2- EaTasa AlS~uboHu , (S, O, K,) inf. n. EaTosN , (TA,) (tropical:) The dawn broke: (S, K:) or shone forth. (K.) [See also gaTasa .]

definition: A swift she-camel;
sourceDefinition: A swift she-camel; as also hayohalapN ; (S, O, K;) and so ↓ EayohuwlN and ↓ EayohaAlN : (IDrd, * O, * K:) or all signify an excellent, strong, she-camel: (K:) or EayohalN signifies a large, big, she-camel; or a tall she-camel: (TA:) [see an ex. in a verse cited in the first paragraph of art. jhm :] and it is also applied to the male of camels, (K, TA,) as some say; (TA;) and EayohalapN to the female; (K, TA;) but, (TA,) accord. to AHát, one should not say jamalN EayohalN ; (S, O, TA;) and some say that one should apply to a she-camel the epithet EayohalapN only: (TA:) sometimes, by poetic license, they said Eayohal~N . (TA.) ― -b3- And the former, A tall woman: (K, TA:) or a strong woman. (TA.) ― -b4- And EayohalapN An old, aged, woman. (O, K, * TA.) ― -b5- And riyHN EayohalN A strong, or violent, wind. (S, O, K. *) ― -b6- EayaAhilu [a pl., of which the sing. is probably EayohalN or EayohalapN ,] see in the first paragraph.

definition: , (S, A, O, TA,) and lahu , and fiyhi , (TA,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, A, O, TA,) and lahu , and fiyhi , (TA,) aor. yaEuwdu , (S, O,) inf. n. EawodN and EawodapN , (S, O, K, TA,) which latter is also an inf. n. of un., (TA,) and maEaAdN , (K, TA,) He, or it, returned to it, (S, A, O, K, * TA,) namely, a thing: (TA:) or, accord. to some, the verb is differently used with fiY and with other preps.: (MF, TA:) [with fY it seems generally to imply some degree of continuance, in addition to the simple meaning of the verb alone:] one says, EAd Alkalobu fiY qayoy^ihi The dog returned to his vomit: (Msb in art. rjE :) and EAd lahu baEoda maA kaAna A^aEoraDa Eanohu [ He returned to it after he had turned away from it ]: (S, O:) and ↓ AiEotaAda , also, signifies he returned: (KL:) or EAd A_ilaY ka*aA , and lahu , inf. n. EawodN (Mgh, Msb) and EawodapN , (Msb,) signifies He, or it, came to such a thing or state or condition; syn. SaAra A_ilyohi ; (Mgh, * Msb;) at first, or for the first time, or originally; and also, a second time, or again; and the verb is trans. by means of EalaY and fiY as well as A_ilaY and li , and also by itself: (Mgh:) lataEuwdun~a fiY mil~atinaA , in the Kur [vii. 86 and xiv. 16], means Ye shall assuredly come to our religion; for the words relate to the apostle: (O, * and Bd in xiv. 16:) or the words relate to the apostle and to those who believed with him, the latter being made to have a predominant influence upon the verb; (Bd in vii. 86 and xiv. 16, and Jel in vii. 86;) the meaning being ye shall assuredly return to our religion: (Bd * and Jel in vii. 86:) or the meaning is, ye shall assuredly enter the communion of our religion; the verb here signifying beginning: and the saying, of a poet, waEaAda Alr~aA^osu min~iY kaAlv~agaAmi is cited as an ex. [i. e. as meaning And my head began to be white like the plant called vgAm ]: or the meaning in this instance may be, became like the vgAm : (MF, TA:) you say also, EAd ka*aA He, or it, became so, or in such a state or condition: (K, TA:) and it is said in a trad., wadidotu A^an~a h`*aA All~abana yaEuwdu qaTiraAnFA [ I wish that this milk would become tar ]. (O, TA.) EAd is also used as an incomplete [i. e. a non-attributive] verb in the sense of kaAna [ He, or it, was ], requiring an enunciative [generally] on the condition of its being preceded by a conjunction, as in the saying of Hassán, walaqado Sabawotu bihaA waEaAda $abaAbuhaA gaD~FA waEaAda zamaAnuhaA musotaZorafFA [ And I had inclined to silly and youthful conduct with her, when her youth was fresh and her time of life was deemed comely ]; the meaning being kaAna $abaAbuhaA [and kaAna zamaAnuhaA ]. (MF, TA.) [See also an ex. in a verse cited voce maTomaEapN . But the first of the significations mentioned in this art. is that which is most common. Hence several phrases mentioned below voce EawodN . And hence the phrase yaEuwdu EalaY ka*aA , inf. n. EawodN , used by grammarians, It refers, or relates, to such a thing; as a pronoun to a preceding noun. Hence, likewise,] ― -b2- EaAdahu is also syn. with AiEotaAdahu , q. v. (S, O.) ― -b3- [Hence, also,] EAd , (Az, TA,) inf. n. EawodN (Az, K, TA) and EiyaAdN , (K,) He repeated, or did a second time. (Az, K, * TA.) One says, badaA^a vum~a EaAda He began, or did a first time, or the first time: then repeated, or did a second time. (Az, TA.) It is said in a prov., AlEawodu A^aHomadu [ Repetition is more praiseworthy: see art. Hmd ]. (S, O.) See also 4, in two places. ― -b4- And Eudotuhu , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. A^aEuwduhu , (S, O,) inf. n. EiyaAdapN (S, O, Msb, K) and EiyaAdN and EawodN and EuwaAdapN (K) and EayoduwdapN [like kayonuwnapN ], (MF,) [ I came to him time after time: see its act. part. n., EaAy^idN :] I visited him, (Msb, K, TA,) [commonly and especially (see again EaAy^idN )] meaning a sick person. (S, O, Msb, K, TA.) ― -b5- EaAdaniY Al$~aYo'u , (TA,) inf. n. EawodN ; (K;) and ↓ AiEotaAdaniY , (TA,) inf. n. AiEotiyaAdN ; (K;) The thing befell me, betided me, or happened to me. (K, * TA.) One says, ham~N waHuzonN ↓ AiEotaAdaniY [ Anxiety and grief betided me ]. (TA.) ― -b6- EaAd bimaEoruwfK , aor. yaEuwdu , inf. n. EawodN , He conferred, or bestowed, favour, or a favour or benefit. (Msb.) One says, EAd EalayonaA fulaAnN bimaEoruwfihi [ Such a one conferred, or bestowed, his favour upon us ]. (A.) And EAd Ealayohi biSilapK [ He conferred, or bestowed, a free gift upon him ]. (TA.) And EAd Ealayohi biAlEaAy^idapi AlS~aAliHapi , aor. yaEuwdu , [meaning It brought him that which was a good return or profit, ] is said of a thing purchased with the price of another thing. (S. and K in art. rjE .) ― -b7- EAd Ealayohimu Ald~ahoru Fortune destroyed them. (A.) And EaAdat Alr~iyaAHu waAlA^amoTaAru EalaY Ald~iyaAri Hat~aY darasato [ The winds and the rains assailed the dwellings so that they became effaced ]. (A.) ― -b8- EawodN is also syn. with rad~N : (K, TA:) one says EAd , inf. n. EawodN , meaning He rejected ( rad~a ) and undid ( naqaDa ) what he had done [as though he reverted from it]. (TA.) [Accord. to the TK, one says, EAd Als~aAy^ila , meaning rad~ahu , i. e. He turned back, or away, the beggar, or asker. ] ― -b9- And i. q. SarofN : (K:) one says, EaAdaniY A^ano A^ajiyoy^aka , in which EAdnY is [said to be] formed by transposition from EadaAniY , meaning He, or it, diverted me from coming to thee: mentioned by Yaakoob. (TA.)

definition: (O, K) He returned it, or restored it, (K,) A_ilaY makaAnihi [ to its place;
sourceDefinition: (O, K) He returned it, or restored it, (K,) A_ilaY makaAnihi [ to its place; he replaced it ]. (O, K.) ― -b2- And He did it a second time: (S, Msb:) he repeated it, or iterated it; syn. kar~arahu ; namely, speech; (K;) as also lahu ↓ EaAda ; he said it a second time; (Mgh;) and A_ilayohi ↓ EAd and Ealayohi [likewise] signify the same as AEAdhu : (TA:) but Aboo-Hilál El-'Askeree says that kar~arahu signifies he repeated it once or more than once; whereas AEAdhu signifies only he repeated it once: (MF, TA:) AEAd AlkalaAma mean he repeated the speech [ saying it ] a second time; syn. rad~adahu vaAniyFA . (O.) One says, AEAd AlS~alaApa He said the prayer a second time. (Msb.) And maA yubodiy^u wamaA yuEiydu signifies mA yatakal~amu bibaAdiy^apK walaA EaAy^idapK , (Lth, A, O,) i. e. He does not say anything for the first time; nor anything for the second time; or anything original, nor anything in the way of repetition; baAdiy^apu AlkalaAmi signifying what is said for the first time; and AlkalaAmi ↓ EaAy^idapu , what is said for the second time, afterwards: (TA in art. bdA^ :) or he says not anything: (A:) and he has no art, artifice, or cunning. (IAar, TA; and A in art. bdA^ ; q. v.) ― -b3- [Also He returned it, or restored it, to a former state: and hence, he renewed it: he reproduced it. ] One says of God, yubodiy^u Alxaloqa vum~a yuEiyduhu , meaning [ He createth, or bringeth into existence, mankind: ] then He returneth them, after life, to lifelessness, in the present world; and after lifelessness, to life, on the day of resurrection. (TA.) ― -b4- See also 8. ― -b5- [ AEAd also signifies He, or it, rendered; or made to be, or become; (like jaEala ;) in which sense it is doubly trans.: see an ex. in a verse cited voce EasiyfN .]

sourceDefinition: , indecl., with kesr for its termination, is a particle in the sense of A_in~a , governing an accus. case, on the condition of its being preceded by a verbal proposition and a conjunction; as in the saying, raqadotu waEaAdi A^abaAka saAhirN [ I slept, and verily thy father was waking, or remaining awake, by night ]: ― -b2- it is also an interrogative particle in the sense of halo , indecl., with kesr for its termination, requiring an answer; as in the saying, EaAdi A^abuwka muqiymN [ Is thy father abiding? ]: ― -b3- it also denotes an answer, in the sense of a proposition rendered negative by means of lm or of mA , only; indecl., with kesr for its termination; and this is when it is conjoined with a pronoun; as when an interrogator says, halo Sal~ayota [ Didst thou perform, or hast thou performed, the act of prayer? ], and thou answerest, EaAdininY , meaning Verily I ( A_in~aniY ) did not perform, or have not performed, the act of prayer: ― -b4- and some of the people of El-Hijáz suppress the n in EaAdiniY : both the modes are chaste when EaAdi is used in the sense of A_in~a : ― -b5- sometimes, also, it is used by the interrogator and the answerer; the former saying, EaAdi xaraja zayodN [ Did Zeyd go forth? or has Zeyd gone forth? ], and the latter saying, EaAdihi , meaning Verily he did not go forth, or has not gone forth: ― -b6- all this is unmentioned by the leading authors on the Arabic language, those of lengthy compositions as well as the epitomisers. (MF, TA.)

rawSourceText: , indecl., with kesr for its termination, is a particle in the sense of A_in~a , governing an accus. case, on the condition of its being preceded by a verbal proposition and a conjunction; as in the saying, raqadotu waEaAdi A^abaAka saAhirN [ I slept, and verily thy father was waking, or remaining awake, by night ]: ― -b2- it is also an interrogative particle in the sense of halo , indecl., with kesr for its termination, requiring an answer; as in the saying, EaAdi A^abuwka muqiymN [ Is thy father abiding? ]: ― -b3- it also denotes an answer, in the sense of a proposition rendered negative by means of lm or of mA , only; indecl., with kesr for its termination; and this is when it is conjoined with a pronoun; as when an interrogator says, halo Sal~ayota [ Didst thou perform, or hast thou performed, the act of prayer? ], and thou answerest, EaAdininY , meaning Verily I ( A_in~aniY ) did not perform, or have not performed, the act of prayer: ― -b4- and some of the people of El-Hijáz suppress the n in EaAdiniY : both the modes are chaste when EaAdi is used in the sense of A_in~a : ― -b5- sometimes, also, it is used by the interrogator and the answerer; the former saying, EaAdi xaraja zayodN [ Did Zeyd go forth? or has Zeyd gone forth? ], and the latter saying, EaAdihi , meaning Verily he did not go forth, or has not gone forth: ― -b6- all this is unmentioned by the leading authors on the Arabic language, those of lengthy compositions as well as the epitomisers. And another says, EawodN EalaY EawodK EalaY EawodK xalaqo i. e. An old man upon an old camel upon an old worn road. (IB, TA.) [See also EaAdiY~N .] ― -b5- And A_in~aka latamut~u biraHimK EawodapK occurs in a trad., as said by Mo'áwiyeh, meaning [ Verily thou seekest to advance thyself in my favour ] by an old and remote tie of relationship. (TA.)

definition: Wood; timber; syn. xa$abN : (Mgh, O, K:) any slender piece of wood or timber: (Lth, TA:) or a piece of wood of any tree, whether slender or thick: or a part, of a tree, in which sap runs, whether...
sourceDefinition: Wood; timber; syn. xa$abN : (Mgh, O, K:) any slender piece of wood or timber: (Lth, TA:) or a piece of wood of any tree, whether slender or thick: or a part, of a tree, in which sap runs, whether fresh and moist or dry: (TA:) a staff; a stick; a rod: and also a sprig: (the lexicons &c. passim:) a branch; or twig; properly, that is cut off; but also applied to one not cut off: (Har p. 499:) [and the stem of the raceme of a palm-tree, and the like: (see faj~aAnN , in art. fj :)] pl. [of mult.] EiydaAnN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) originally EiwodaAnN , (Msb,) and [of pauc.] A^aEowaAdN . (S, O, Msb, K.) ― -b2- [Hence,] rak~aba A@ll~`hu EuwdFA EuwdFA , (A,) or EuwdFA EalaY EuwdK , (TA,) God caused the arrow to be put upon the bow, for shooting; (A;) meaning that civil war, or conflict, or faction, or sedition, became excited. (A, TA.) ― -b3- And sabiylu *iY AlA^aEowaAdi (assumed tropical:) Death: AlAEwAd meaning the pieces of wood upon which the dead is carried: (El-Mufaddal, Az, L:) for the Arabs of the desert, having no biers, put two pieces of wood together, and on them carry the dead to the grave. (Az, L.) ― -b4- And AlEuwdaAni The pulpit and the staff of the Prophet. (Sh, O, K.) ― -b5- And one says, huwa Sulobu AlEuwdi : (tropical:) see art. Slb . ― -b6- And huwo mino Euwdi SidoqK and sawo'K (tropical:) [ He is of a good branch and of a bad branch ]. (TA.) ― -b7- And it is said in a trad. of Shureyh, A_in~amaA AlqaDaA='u jamorN faA@dofaEi Aljamora Eanoka biEuwdayoni [ Verily the exercise of the judicial office is like the approaching live coals; and repel thou the live coals from thee by means of two sticks ]: meaning, guard thyself well from the fire [of Hell] by means of two witnesses; like as he who warms himself by means of fire repels the live coals from his place with a stick or other thing that he may not be burned: or act firmly and deliberately in judging, and do thy utmost to repel from thee the fire [of Hell]. (L.) ― -b8- Euwdu AlS~aliybi : see yaboruwHN . ― -b9- AlEuwdu also signifies [ Aloes-wood; ] a well-known odoriferous substance; (Msb;) that with which one fumigates himself; (S, O, K; *) a certain aromatized wood, with which one fumigates himself; thus called because of its excellence: (L:) AlEuwdu AlhinodiY~u [which, like Euwdu Albaxuwri and Euwdu Aln~ad~i and AlEuwdu AlqamaAriY~u and AlEuwdu AlquAqul~iY~u , is a common, well-known, term for aloes-wood,] is said to be the same as AlqusoTu AlbaHoriY~u . (TA. [See art. qsT .]) ― -b10- And A certain musical instrument, (S, O, L, Msb, K,) well known; (TA;) [ the lute; which word, like the French “ luth,” &c., is derived from AlEuwd : accord. to the L, it has four chords; but I have invariably found it to have seven double chords: it is figured and described in my work on the Modern Egyptians: in the present day it is generally played with a plectrum, formed of a slip of a vulture's feather; but in former times it seems to have been usually played upon with the tips of the fingers:] pl. as above, EiydaAnN and A^aEowaAdN . (Msb.) ― -b11- And The bone [ called os hyoides ] at the root of the tongue; (O, K;) also called Euwdu All~isaAni . (O.) ― -b12- And A^um~u AlEuwdi signifies The [ portion, or appertenance, of the stomach of a ruminant animal, called ] qibap , (O,) or qib~ap , (K,) i. e. the faHiv : (TA:) pl. A^um~ahaAtu AlEuwdi . (O.)

sourceDefinition: , originally EiwodN , the w being changed into Y because of the kesreh before it, (Az, TA,) An occurrence that befalls, or betides, one, or that happens to one, [or returns to one, of some former affection of the mind or body, i. e.] of anxiety, (S, O, K,) or of some other kind, (S, O,) of disease, or of grief, (O, K,) and the like, (K,) of affliction, and of desire: and accord. to Az, the time of return of joy and of grief. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence, A festival; or periodical festival; ] a feast-day; (KL;) i. q. mawosimN ; (Msb;) any day on which is an assembling, or a congregating; (K;) [and particularly an anniversary festival: ] so called because it returns every year with renewed joy: (IAar, TA:) or, from EaAda , because people return to it: or from EaAdapN , “ a custom,” because they are accustomed to it: (TA:) pl. A^aEoyaAdN ; the Y being retained in the pl. because it is in the sing., or to distinguish it from A^aEowaAdN the pl. of EuwdN ; (S, O, Msb;) for regularly its pl. would be A^aEowaAdN , like as A^arowaAHN is pl. of riyHN . (TA.) [The two principal religious festivals of the Muslims are called Eiydu AlA^aDoHaY The festival of the victims (see art. DHw and DHY ) and Eiydu AlfiTori The festival of the breaking of the fast after Ramadán.] The dim. of EiydN is ↓ EuyayodN ; the Y being retained in it like as it is retained in the pl. (TA.) ― -b3- See also EaAdapN , in two places. -A2- Also, A certain sort of mountain-tree, (K, TA,) that produces twigs about a cubit in length, dust- coloured, having no leaves nor blossoms, but having much peel, and having many knots: fresh wounds are dressed with its peel, and close up in consequence thereof. (TA.)

definition: , signifying Return, is originally maEowadN .

See EawodN , first and third sentences. ― -b2- Also A place to which a person, or thing, returns: a place, state, or result, to which a person, or thing, eventually comes; a place of destination, or an ultimate state or condition: syn. marojiEN : and maSiyrN . (S, A, O, K.) ― -b3- [Hence,] AlmaEaAdu signifies [particularly] The ultimate state of existence, in the world to come; syn. AlA=xirapu ; (M, K, TA;) [and] so maEaAdu Alxaloqi : (S, O:) the place to which one comes on the day of resurrection. (TA.) And Paradise. (K.) And Mekkeh: (O, K:) the conquest of which was promised to the Prophet: (TA:) so called because the pilgrims return to it. (O.) laraAd~uka A_ilaY maEaAdK , in the Kur [xxviii. 85], is expl. as meaning will assuredly return thee, or restore thee, to Mekkeh: (O, K:) or mEAd here means Paradise: (K:) or thy fixed place in Paradise: (I'Ab, TA:) or the place of thy birth: (Fr, TA:) or thy home and town: (Th, TA:) or thy usual state in which thou wast born: or thy original condition among the sons of Háshim: or, accord. to most of the expositors, the words mean will assuredly raise thee from the dead. (TA.) ― -b4- And The pilgrimage. (K.) ― -b5- And maEaAdN (Lth, TA) and ↓ maEaAdapN (Lth, A, TA) A place of wailing for a dead person: (Lth, A, TA:) so called because people return to it time after time: (Lth, * A:) pl. maEaAwidu . (A.) [Hence,] one says, ↓ liA=li fulaAnK maEaAdapN , meaning An affliction has happened to the family of such a one, the people coming to them in the places of wailing for the dead, or in other places, and the women talking of him. (Lth, TA.)

[Hence,] AlmaEaAdu signifies [particularly] The ultimate state of existence, in the world to come; syn. And Mekkeh: (O, K:) the conquest of which was promised to the Prophet: (TA:) so called because the pilgrims return to it. (O.) laraAd~uka A_ilaY maEaAdK , in the Kur [xxviii. 85], is expl. as meaning will assuredly return thee, or restore thee, to Mekke...
And The pilgrimage. (K.)

And maEaAdN (Lth, TA) and ↓ maEaAdapN (Lth, A, TA) A place of wailing for a dead person: (Lth, A, TA:) so called because people return to it time after time: (Lth, * A:) pl. maEaAwidu . (A.) [Hence,] one says, ↓ liA=li fulaAnK maEaAdapN , meaning An affliction has happened to the family of such a one, the people coming to them in the places of wailing for the dead, or in other places, and the women talking of him. (Lth, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yagur~u , inf. n. guruwrN (Fr, S, Msb, K) and gar~N , (Az, K,) which latter is preferable to the former, [though less common,] because the inf. n. of a trans. verb is scarcely ever of the measure fuEuwlN , (Az,) and gir~apN (Lh, K) and gararN , (IKtt, TA,) He (the devil, TA) deceived him; beguiled him; (S, K;) made him to desire what was vain, or false. (K.) You say gar~atohu Ald~unoyaA The world deceived him, or beguiled him, by its finery, or show, or pomp. (Msb.) It is said in the Kur [lxxxii. 6], maA gar~aka birab~ika What hath deceived thee, and led thee into error, so that thou hast neglected what was incumbent on thee to thy Lord? (Aboo-Is-hák:) or what hath deceived thee respecting thy Lord, and induced thee to disobey Him, and to feel secure from his punishment? (TA:) or what hath deceived thee, and emboldened thee to disobey thy Lord? (Bd. [But see bi as syn. with Eano .]) maA gar~aka bifulaAnK signifies [ What hath deceived thee, and emboldened thee against such a one? or] how is it that thou art emboldened against such a one? (As, S, Msb, TA.) [See also 4.] And mano gar~aka bifulaAnK , (TA,) and mino fulaAnK , (S, TA,) Who hath made thee to pursue a course without being rightly directed, or a course not plain, ( mano A^awoTaA^aka Eu$owapF , S, TA,) with respect to such a one, (S,) or with respect to the case of such a one? (TA. [See again 4.]) [Also gur~a mino fulaAnK , i. e. gur~a guruwrFA SaAdirFA mino fulaAnK , He was deceived by such a one; he was deceived with deceit proceeding from such a one. See gariyrN , as syn. with magoruwrN .] And gar~a fulaAnN fulaAnFA Such a one exposed such a one to perdition or destruction [app. by deceiving him ]. (TA. [See also 2, and 4.]) Also Such a one acted with such a one in a manner resembling the slaying with the edge of the sword. (TA. [See 3 in art. ETw .]) -A2- gar~a faroxahu , (S, O, K,) aor. , (S, O,) inf. n. gar~N (S, O, K) and giraArN , (O, K, [or the latter is inf. n. of gaAr~a only,]) It (a bird, S, O, K, * or a pigeon, TA) fed its young one with its bill: (S, O, K:) and A^unovaAhu ↓ gAr~ , (As, S, K,) inf. n. giraArN (S) or mugaAr~apN , (TA,) he (the [collared turtle-dove called] qumoriY~ ) fed his female with his bill. (As, S, K.) ― -b2- Hence, in a trad., kaAna yagur~u Ealiy~FA (O, TA) biAlEilomi (TA) (assumed tropical:) He (the Prophet) used to nourish 'Alee with knowledge like as the bird feeds its young one. (O, TA. *) And one says, gur~a fulaAnN mina AlEilomi maA lamo yugar~uhu gayoruhu (assumed tropical:) Such a one has been nourished, and instructed, with that wherewith other than he has not been nourished, and instructed, of knowledge. (TA.) -A3- gar~a , aor. yagir~u , (S, Msb,) with kesr; (S;) or gar~a , see. pers. garirota , aor. yagar~u ; (K, TA;) inf. n. garaArapN ; (S, Msb, K;) He (a man, S, Msb, or a youth, or young man, K) was inexperienced in affairs; (S, K;) he was ignorant of affairs; negligent, or heedless, of them. (Msb.) You say kaAna *`lika fiY garaAratiY waHadaAvatiY , i. e. fiY gir~atiY , That was in [the time of] my inexperience and youth. (S.) [See also 8.] ― -b2- And gar~a , (K,) see. pers. garrota , (IAar, T, TA,) aor. yagar~u , with fet-h, (IAar, T, K,) inf. n. garaArapN , (IAar, T, TA,) He acted in a youthful or childish manner: (IAar, T, TA:) or he so acted after having soundness of judgment, produced by experience. (Sgh, K.) But this is at variance with what J cites from Fr, in art. $d , that the aor. of an intrans. verb of this class of the measure faEala , should be of the measure yafoEilu , with kesr to the E . (TA.) -A4- gar~a , (IAar, IKtt, K,) in one place written by IAar garira , to show that it is of the measure faEila , and that the sec. pers. is garirota , (TA,) aor. yagar~u , (IAar, IKtt, K,) inf. n. gararN (IAar, K) and gur~apN , (IAar, IKtt, K,) or the latter, as ISd thinks, is not an inf. n., but a subst., (TA,) and garAarapN , (K,) He (a horse, IAar, IKtt, and a camel, IAar) had what is termed a gur~ap upon his forehead: (IAar, IKtt:) it (his face) had what is so termed: (K:) it (his face) became white. (IAar, K. *) ― -b2- gar~a , aor. yagar~u , He (a man) became eminent, or noble. (TA.) ― -b3- And gur~apN signifies also A grape-vine's quickly becoming tall. (K.) -A5- See also R. Q. 1. -A6- gar~a Ealayohi AlmaA='a He poured upon him, or it, the water: like qar~a . (TA.) And gur~a fiY HawoDika Pour thou into thy watering-trough. (TA.) And gur~a fiY siqaAy^ika Fill thou thy skin by putting it into the water and throwing the water into it with thy hand, not abstaining until thou fillest it: thus as related by Az accord. to the usage of the desert-Arabs. (TA.)

definition: He, or it, emboldened him, or encouraged him;
sourceDefinition: He, or it, emboldened him, or encouraged him; [ by deceiving him; ] syn. A^ajosarahu : so says AHeyth; and he cites the following verse: A^agar~a hi$aAmFA mino A^axiyhi A@boni A^um~ihi qawaAdimu SaA^onK yas~arato warabiyEu meaning [ The teats of sheep that have yielded abundance of milk and of young, and spring herbage, i. e.] the abundance of his sheep and their milk, have emboldened Hishám against his brother, the son of his mother, [to pursue a wrong course towards him, and] to forsake him, thinking himself in dependent of him: the poet makes qwAdm to belong to sheep, whereas they properly belong to the udders of camels, using the word metaphorically. (TA.) [But I incline to think that the A^a in A^agar~a is the interrogative particle, and that its explanation is A^ajas~ara , with the same particle; and the more so as I have not found any authority, if this be not one, for A^ajosara in the sense of jas~ara : so that the meaning of the verse is, Have the teats, &c.? and it shows that gar~ahu minohu , not A^agar~ahu , means jas~arahu Ealayohi , like gar~ahu bihi . See 1.] ― -b2- Also He caused him to fall into peril, danger, jeopardy, hazard, or risk. (TA.) [But perhaps this meaning is also derived from a misunderstanding of the verse quoted above. See again 1.]

definition: Inexperienced in affairs;
sourceDefinition: Inexperienced in affairs; (S, K;) ignorant of affairs; negligent, or heedless, of them; (Msb;) applied to a man, (S, Msb,) or to a youth, or young man; (K;) as also ↓ gaAr~N (Msb) and ↓ gariyrN ; (S, K;) and applied to a young woman; as also gir~apN and ↓ gariyrapN (S, K:) or these three epithets, applied to a girl, signify young, inexperienced in affairs, and not knowing what woman know of love: (A'Obeyd:) the pl. of gir~N is A^agoraArN (S) and giraArN ; (TA;) and of ↓ gariyrN , A^agor~aA='u (S, K) and A^agir~apN [which is a pl. of pane.] (K.) [And gir~apN is also used as a pl.] Paradise says, yado xuloniY gir~apu Aln~aAsi The simple, of mankind, who prefer obscurity. and discard the affairs of the present world, and provide themselves for the world to come, enter me. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b2- Also Youthful, or childish, in conduct: applied to a man, and to a girl, or young woman. (IAar, T.) ― -b3- And One who submits to be deceived. (K.)

definition: Whiteness: clearness of colour or complexion.
sourceDefinition: Whiteness: clearness of colour or complexion. (L, TA.) So in the phrase gur~apF ↓ A^agar~u [app. meaning More, or most. fair-complexioned ]; occurring in a trad. applied to virgins: or the phrase is ↓ gir~apF ↓ A^agar~u , meaning more, or most, remote from the knowledge of evil. (L.) ― -b2- [ A star, or blaze, or white mark, on the forehead or face of a horse; ] a whiteness on the forehead of a horse, (S, Mgh, Msb, K, *) above the size of a diroham ; (S, Msb;) or of the size of a drhm ; (Mgh;) as also ↓ gurogurapN : (S, K:) or it is a general term [ for a star or blaze ], including different kinds, as the quroHap and the $imoraAx and the like: or, if round, it is termed watiyrapN ; and if long, $aAdixapN : or as, ISd thinks, the space itself, of the face, that is occupied by whiteness; not the whiteness: pl. gurarN . (TA.) [See also A^agar~u .] ― -b3- In a dog, A white speck, or a small white spot, above each of the eyes: so in a trad., in which it is said that the black dog having two such marks is to be killed. (TA.) -A2- Also (tropical:) The first, or commencement, of the month; (Msb;) the night, of the month, in which the new moon is first seen: (K:) so called as being likened to the gur~ap on the forehead of a horse: (AHeyth:) pl. gurarN : (AHeyth, Msb:) which is also applied to the first three nights of the month. (A'Obeyd, S, Msb.) One says katabotu gur~apa Al$~ahori ka*aA I wrote on the first of the month thus. (TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] (assumed tropical:) The first, or commencement, of El-Islám; (TA;) and of anything. (S.) ― -b3- The whiteness of the teeth; and the [ first that appears ] of them. (K.) ― -b4- (assumed tropical:) The head app. when first appearing ] of a plant. (TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) [The sight, or spectacle, or] whatever appears to one, of light, or daybreak: you say thereof, badato gur~atuhu [ The sight, or spectacle, thereof appeared ]. (K.) ― -b6- (assumed tropical:) The aspect of the new moon: (K:) because of its whiteness: (TA:) or the phasis of the moon in the first night of the month ]. (TA in art. hl .) ― -b7- (assumed tropical:) The face of a man: (K:) or his aspect; syn. TaloEap . (TA.) ― -b8- (assumed tropical:) [And The forehead of a man. So used, as opposed to qafFA , in the Life of Teemoor, 170, ed. Mang., cited by Freytag; and so used in the present day; but whether in classical times I know not.] ― -b9- taTowiylu Algur~api . in performing the ablution termed waDuwo' , means (assumed tropical:) The washing of the fore part of the head with the face, and the washing of the side of the neck: or, as some say the washing of somewhat of the fore arm and of the shank with the hand and the foot. (Msb) ― -b10- And gur~ahN also signifies (assumed tropical:) A noble, or an eminent man, (K,) or a chief, or lord, (S,) of a people (S, K:) pl. gurarN . (S.) ― -b11- And (tropical:) The best. (K.) and chiefest, (TA,) of goods. or household furniture: (K:) pl. as above: (TA:) the best of anything: (S:) the best, (Mgh,) or most precious and excellent, (Aboo-Sa'eed,) of property ; as, for instance, a horse, and an excellent camel, (Aboo-Sa'eed, Mgh.) and camels, (TA.) and a male slave. (Aboo-Sa'eed. S. Mgh, Msb, K.) and a female slave, (S, Msb, K,) or a clever female slave: (Aboo-Sa'eed, Mgh:) its application to a slave, male or female, [among articles of property,] is most common. (TA.) It has this last signification (a male or female slave) in a trad. in which it relates to the compensation for the destroying of a child in the womb: (TA:) as though this term were applied, by a synecdoche, to the whole person; (S;) the word properly signifying the “ face; ” in like manner as the terms raqabapN and raA^osN are employed: (Mgh:) Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-Alà is related to have said that it there means a white male slave or a white female slave: but this is not a condition accord. to the doctors of practical law; for they hold the term to mean a male or female slave whose price amounts to the tenth part of the whole price of blood: (IAth:) or to the twentieth part thereof: (K, T:) or it means a slave of the best sort. (Mgh.) The Rájiz says, kul~u qatiylK fiY kulayobK gur~aho Hat~aY yanaAla Alqatolu A=la mur~aho Every one slain in retaliation for Kuleyb is as a slave, until the slaying reach the family of Mur- rah. (TA.) ― -b12- Also (assumed tropical:) Goodness, and righteous conduct: so in the saying, A_iy~aAkumo waAlmu$Aar~apa faA_in~ahaA tadofinu Algur~apa watuZohiru AlEur~apa [ Avoid ye contention, or disputation, for it hides goodness, &c., and manifests what is disgraceful ]. (TA.) -A3- [It is also an inf. n.: see 1, latter part.]

definition: Very deceitful; applied in this sense as an epithet to the present world; (Msb;) or what deceives one; (K;) such as a man, and a devil, or other thing; (As, TA;) or such as property or wealth, and...
sourceDefinition: Very deceitful; applied in this sense as an epithet to the present world; (Msb;) or what deceives one; (K;) such as a man, and a devil, or other thing; (As, TA;) or such as property or wealth, and rank or station, and desire, and a devil: (B, TA:) and ↓ guruwrN signifies a thing by which one is deceived, of worldly goods or advantages: (S:) or the former signifies the devil, specially; (Yaakoob, S, K;) because he deceives men by false promises and by inspiring hopes; or because he urges a man to do those things which are causes of his being loved but which are followed by that which grieves him: (TA:) and this last sense it has, accord. to ISk, in the Kur xxxi. 33 and xxxv. 5: (S:) also the present world; (K;) as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates: and this sense is assigned to it by some as used in the passages of the Kur-án to which reference has just been made. (TA.) [It is masc. and fem., agreeably with analogy.] -A2- Also A medicine with which one gargles: (S, K:) a word similar to laduwdN and laEuwqN and saEuwTN (S) and safuwfN . (TA.)

definition: Deceived; beguiled; made to desire what is vain, or false; (A'Obeyd, K;) and so ↓ magoruwrN . (K.) And you say likewise, minoka ↓ A^anaA gararN , in the sense of magoruwrN [ I am deceived by thee ]....
sourceDefinition: Deceived; beguiled; made to desire what is vain, or false; (A'Obeyd, K;) and so ↓ magoruwrN . (K.) And you say likewise, minoka ↓ A^anaA gararN , in the sense of magoruwrN [ I am deceived by thee ]. (TA.) And ↓ magoruwrN signifies also A man who marries to a woman in the belief that she is free, and finds her to be a slave. (TA.) ― -b2- See also gir~N , in three places. ― -b3- It is said in a prov., A^anaA gariyruka mino h`*aA AlA^amori , meaning I am one possessing knowledge in this affair so that when thou askest me of it I will inform thee respecting it without being prepared for it and without consideration: so says AZ: and Z says the like; i. e. I [ am one who ] will answer thee if thou ask me unexpectedly respecting this affair by reason of the soundness of my knowledge of the true state of the case: or [it means I am a deceived informant of thee respecting this affair; for] as As says, the meaning is, thou art not deceived by me, but I am the person deceived; the case being this, that false information came to me, and I acquainted thee with it, and it was not as I told thee; I having only related what I had heard. (TA.) And one says, A^anaA gariyruka minohu i. e. I caution thee [or I am thy cautioner ] against him; (K, TA:) [i. e.,] mino fulaAnK [ against such a one ]; (S, O;) meaning, as Aboo-Nasr says in the “ Kitáb el-Ajnás, ” [ that ] there shall not happen to thee, from him, that whereby thou shalt be deceived; (S, O, TA;) as though he said, I am thy surety, or sponsor, for that. (AM, TA.) ― -b4- [Hence, app., it is said that] gariyrN signifies also A surety, sponsor, or guarantee. (K, TA.) ― -b5- And Eayo$N gariyrN (tropical:) A life in which one is not made to be in fear: (S, K, TA:) like Eayo$N A^abolahu : (TA:) pl. gur~aAnN . (K.) ― -b6- Hence, perhaps; or from Algir~apu [app. as meaning “ inexperience ”], which is sometimes approved; (Har p. 607;) or because it [sometimes] deceives; (TA;) gariyrN also signifies (tropical:) Good disposition or nature. (S, O, K, TA.) One says of a man when he has become old, and evil in disposition, A^adobara gariyruhu waA^aqobala hariyruhu (tropical:) His good disposition has regressed, or departed, and his evil disposition has advanced, or come: (S, Meyd, O, TA:) or what deceived and pleased has gone from him, and what is disliked on his part, of evilness of disposition &c., has come. (Meyd.)

sourceDefinition: (S, &c.) Thick, gross, big, bulky, or coarse; (Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ gulaAZN : (K:) fem. of the former with p : (TA:) and pl. gilaAZN . (Msb, TA.) Applied [to a body, &c.; and, as meaning Thick, or coarse, ] to a garment, or piece of cloth. (Mgh, K.) You say also, A^aroDN galiyZapN Rough, or rugged, land. (ISd, TA.) [And in this sense, of rough, or rugged, galiyZN is used in relation to various things.] ― -b2- Applied to a colour [ Dense, or deep: see gaDobN ]. (K in art. gDb .) ― -b3- Also, applied to a man, (tropical:) Characterized by giloZap , the contr. of riq~ap , in manners, disposition, action or conduct, speech, life, and the like; rough, coarse, rude, unkind, hard, churlish, uncivil, surly, rough in manners, hard to deal with, incompliant, unobsequious, evil in disposition, illnatured, or the like: (Msb, * TA:) and so galiyZu AljaAnibi ; [ contr. of lay~inu AljaAnibi :] (O and K in art. fZ :) and galiyZu Alqalobi hard-hearted; (Bd in iii. 153;) evil in disposition, or illnatured. (TA.) Applied also to an affair, meaning (tropical:) Hard, or difficult. (TA.) And to punishment, [in the Kur xi. 61, &c.,] meaning (tropical:) Vehement, or severe; (Mgh;) intensely painful. (Msb.) And [in like manner] to slaying and wounding. (TA.) And to a compact, or covenant, [in the Kur iv. 25, &c.,] meaning (tropical:) Strong, confirmed, or ratified. (Mgh, TA.) A poet, cited by El-Muärrij, says, wakaAy^ino taraY mino jaAhilK baEoda Eilomihi ↓ AlhawaY jaholFA Eani AlHaq~i faA@nogawaY ↓ gawaAhu [ How many an ignorant dost thou see, whom, after his knowledge, love, or desire, has urged to turn, in ignorance, from that which was right, and who has turned: or has turned, in ignorance, from that which was right, and who has suffered himself to be turned; for,] accord. to Az, gawaAhu AlhawaY is most correctly rendered as meaning lawaAhu , and Sarafahu ; and AngwY is quasi-pass. thereof. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. , (M,) inf. n. fatonN , (S, M, K,) [and quasi-inf. n., in this and other senses, fitonapN ,] He burned it (T, * S, * M, K *) in the fire. (M.) Hence, [in the Kur li. 13,] yawoma humo EalaY A@ln~aAri yufotanuwna (T, * S, M, K *) i. e. [ The day, or on the day, accord. to two different readings, ( yawomu and yawoma , the latter of which is the more common,)] when they shall be burned (T, S, M, K) with the fire [of Hell]. (T.) And [in the Kur lxxxv. 10,] A_in~a A@l~a*iyna fatanuwA A@lomuw^ominiyna waA@lomuw^ominaAti Verily they who burned the believing men and the believing women (T, S *) in the fire kindled in the trench, or pit; throwing them therein. (T.) This is said to be the primary signification of the verb. (TA.) ― -b2- And He melted it with fire, (T,) or put it into the fire, (S, Msb,) namely, gold, (T, S, Msb,) and silver, in order to separate, or distinguish, (T, Msb,) the bad from the good, (T,) or the good from the bad, (Msb,) or to see what was its [ degree of ] goodness. (S.) ― -b3- And hence, accord. to Er-Rághib, Alfatonu is used as meaning The causing a man to enter into fire [app. by way of trial, or probation ], and [ in like manner ] into a state of punishment, or affliction: (TA:) [and it is also used as meaning the slaying another; whence, in the Kur iv. 102,] A_ino xifotumo A^ano yafotinakumu A@l~a*iyna kafaruwA means [ If ye fear that those who have disbelieved ] may slay you; and in like manner in the Chapter of Yoonus [i. e. in x. 83], A^ano yafotinahumo means An yaqotulahumo . (T. [In the TA, these two exs. are misplaced, or something has been omitted before them by a copyist.]) ― -b4- [Hence also,] one says, fatanahu , aor. , (K, TA,) inf. n. fatonN , (TA,) He, or it, caused him to fall into Alfitonap ; (K, TA;) i. e. trial; and affliction, distress, or hardship; [generally meaning an affliction whereby some good or evil quality is put to the test; ] (TA;) as also ↓ Aifotatanahu ; and ↓ ft~nhu ; (K, TA;) but this, of which the inf. n. is tafotiynN , has an intensive signification; (S;) and ↓ A^afotanahu ; (K, TA;) which last is rare, or rather, accord. to As, [though app. not in this sense, but in another, to be mentioned in what follows,] is not allowable: (TA:) the first of these verbs is trans. and intrans.: (S, K, TA:) you say also, fatana , (AZ, T, S, K, TA,) aor. , (AZ, T, K,) inf. n. futuwnN , (AZ, T, S, TA,) He fell into fitonap [i. e. trial, or affliction, &c.]; (AZ, T, K;) as also ↓ Aifotatana : (K:) or the former signifies he shifted from a good, to an evil, state or condition: or, accord. to En-Nadr, one says ↓ Aifotatana and Aufotutina , both meaning the same; and this is correct; but fatana as quasi-pass. of fatanotuhu [i. e. as intrans.] is of weak authority: (T:) and ↓ Aufotutina , said of a man, [as also Aifotatana ,] and futina , signify the same, (S, M,) accord. to AZ, (M,) i. e. he was smitten by a fitonap [or trial, &c.,] so that his wealth, or property, or his intellect, departed: and likewise he was tried, or tested: (S:) and accord. to AZ, one says, of a man, ↓ A^ufotina , [if not a mistranscription for Aufotutina , as above,] with damm, meaning futina : (TA:) [and fatanahu has futuwnN also as an inf. n.:] it is said in the Kur [xx. 41], wafatan~aAka futuwnFA (S) i. e. And we tried thee with a [ severe ] trying: or the noun in this instance is pl. of fatonN ; or of fitonapN , formed by disregard of the p , like HujuwzN and buduwrN which are [said to be] pls. of HujozapN and badorapN ; so that the meaning is, we tried thee with several sorts of trying: (Bd:) or, as some say, and we purified thee with a [ thorough or an effectual ] purifying [ like that of gold, or silver, by means of fire ]: (TA:) [in many instances] fatanahu , aor. , [inf. n. fatonN ,] signifies He tried, or tested, him; whence, in the Kur ix. 127, yufotanuwna means They are tried, or tested, by being summoned to war, against unbelievers or the like; or, as some say, by the infliction of punishment or of some evil thing. (M.) fatanotumo A^anofusakumo , in the Kur [lvii. 13], means Ye caused yourselves to fall into trial and punishment. (TA.) And wahumo laA yufotanuwna , in the Kur xxix. 1, is expl. as meaning While they are not tried in their persons and their possessions so that he who has true faith may be known from others by his patient endurance of trial. (T.) And the saying, in a trad., A_in~akumo tufotanuwna fiY Alqubuwri means [ Verily ye shall be tried, or tested, in the graves by ] the questioning of [ the two angels ] Munkar and Nekeer. (TA.) [See also mafotuwnN , which is said to be an inf. n., and syn. with fitonapN , meaning xiborapN , or with futuwnN (mentioned above as an inf. n. of the intrans. v. fatana ), meaning junuwnN ; as well as a pass. part. n.] ― -b5- And fatanahN , (M, TA,) inf. n. fatonN , (TA, [or perhaps futuwnN , as in the next following sentence]) also signifies He made him (a man, M) to turn from, or quit, (M, TA,) the predicament in which he was, (M,) or the right course: (TA:) whence, in the Kur [xvii. 75], waA_ino kaAduwA layafotinuwnaka Eani A@l~a*iY A^awoHayonaA A_ilayoka (M, TA) i. e. [ And verily they were near to ] their making thee to turn [ from that which we had revealed to thee ]: thus this saying has been explained. (TA.) [And He, or it, seduced him; or tempted him: thus it may often be well rendered, agreeably with what next precedes and what next follows, and with explanations of its act. part. n. and of fitonapN .] And one says, fatana AlmaAlu Aln~aAsa , aor. , inf. n. futuwnN , [or perhaps fatonN , as in the next preceding sentence,] meaning Wealth, or property, inclined, or attracted, to it, men, or mankind: and futina fiY diynihi and ↓ Aufotutina , both in the pass. form, He declined [or was made to decline ] from [ the right way in ] his religion. (Msb.) And fatanahu , aor, , inf. n. fatonN and futuwnN , (M, K,) He, or it induced in him admiration, or pleasure; (M, * K, * TA;) as also ↓ A^afotanahu [respecting which see what here follows]: (M, K:) and one says, of a woman, fatanatohu , (T, S,) meaning [ She enamoured him; or captivated his heart; i. e.] she bereaved him of his heart, or reason, ( dal~ahatohu , [thus in several copies of the S, in one of my copies bal~ahatohu ,] and [ so affected him that ] he loved her; (S;) as also ↓ A^afotanatohu ; (T, S;) the former of the dial. of El-Hijáz, and the latter of the dial. of Nejd; (T, S; *) but ↓ Aftnthu , (T, S,) or Aftnhu , (M,) was disallowed by As, (T, S, M,) and he paid no regard to a verse mentioned to him as an ex. thereof, (T,) [or] he ignored a verse cited to him as an ex. of the pass. part. n. from an A^urojuwzap of Ru-beh, not knowing it therein; (M;) most of the lexicologists, however, allow both: (T:) Sb says that fatanahu signifies he put [or occasioned ] in him fitonap ; and ↓ Aftnhu , he caused Alfitonap to come to him [or to affect him ]; (M;) or he said that the latter means he made him to be faAtin : (TA voce Hazanahu :) and one says also, of a man, futina bA@lomaroA^api and ↓ Aufotutina [both meaning He was enamoured by the woman ]. (T.) ― -b6- And one says also, of a man, fatana , aor. , inf. n. futuwnN , meaning He desired Alfujuwr [i. e. the committing of adultery or fornication ]: (AZ, TA:) or fatana A_ilaY Aln~isaA='i , inf. n. futuwnN , he desired Alfujuwr (T, M, K, TA) with women or the women; as also futina A_ilayohin~a . (M, K, TA.)

definition: A burning with fire.
sourceDefinition: A burning with fire. (T.) ― -b2- And The melting of gold and of silver (K, TA) in order to separate, or distinguish, the bad from the good. (TA.) ― -b3- And [hence, or] from fatana signifying “ he melted, ” (T,) or from that verb as signifying “ he put into the fire, “ (Msb,) gold, and silver, “ for that purpose, ” (T, Msb,) it signifies A trial, or probation; (IAar, T, S, M, K, TA;) and affliction, distress, or hardship; (TA;) and [particularly] an affliction whereby one is tried, proved, or tested: (IAar, T, S, K, TA:) this is the sum of its meaning in the language of the Arabs: (T, TA: *) or the trial whereby the condition of a man may be evinced: this, accord. to Zj, may be the meaning in the Kur v. 45: (M:) or a mean whereby the condition of a man is evinced, in respect of good and of evil: (Kull:) [hence it often means a temptation: ] and ↓ mafotuwnN signifies the same as fitonapN , (S, M, K,) meaning a trial: (K:) the pl. of fitonapN is fitanN . (Msb.) It proceeds from God and from man: (Er-Rághib, TA:) [there are many instances of its proceeding from God in the Kur; for ex., in xxxvii. 61,] A_in~aA jaEalonaAhaA fitonapF lilZ~aAlimiyna i. e. [ Verily we have made it to be ] a trial [ to the wrongdoers ] is said in relation to the tree Ez-Zakkoom; the existence of which they disbelieved; for when they heard that it comes forth in the bottom of Hell, they said, Trees become burned in the fire; then how can they grow therein? (M.) [And hence] it signifies also Punishment, castigation, or chastisement. (T, M, K.) And Slaughter: (T:) and civil war, or conflict occurring among people: (M:) and slaughter, and war, and faction, or sedition, among the parties of the Muslims when they form themselves into parties: (T:) and discord, dissension, or difference of opinions, among the people. (IAar, T, K.) A misleading; or causing to err, or go astray: (T, K:) [ seduction; or temptation: or a cause thereof; such as ] the ornature, finery, show, or pomp, and the desires, or lusts, of the present life or world, whereby one is tried: (T:) and wealth, or children; (T, K, TA;) because one is tried thereby: (TA:) and women; than whom, the Prophet said, there is no fitonap more harmful to men: (T:) and a cause of one's being pleased with a thing; (T, M, K;) as in the saying laA tajoEalonaA fitonapF liloqawomi A@lZ~aAlimiyna [in the Kur x. 85, i. e. (T.) Also Madness, insanity, or diabolical possession; (T, K;) and so ↓ futuwnN and ↓ mafotuwnN . (T.) And Error; or deviation from the right way. (M, K.) (M, K.) fitonapu AlS~adori signifies AlwasowaAsu [app. as meaning The devil's prompting, or suggesting, of some evil idea ]: fitonapu AlmaHoyaA , The being turned from the [ right ] road: fitonapu AlmamaAti , The being questioned in the grave [by the two angels Munkar and Nekeer]: fitonapu AlD~ur~i , The sword: and fitotapu Als~ur~i , Women. (TA.) sourceDefinition: [pass. part. n. of 1; signifying Burned: &c.]. ― -b2- It is applied as an epithet to a deenár as meaning Put into the fire in order that one may see what is its [ degree of ] goodness. (S.) ― -b3- It signifies also Smitten by a fitonap [or trial, &c.,] so that his wealth, or property, or his intellect, has departed: and likewise tried, or tested: (S:) or caused to fall into Alfitonap ; (K, TA;) i. e. trial; and affliction, distress, or hardship; (TA;) as also ↓ mufotanN . (K, TA.) And [particularly] Afflicted with madness, insanity, or diabolical possession. (T, K. *) [See also what here follows.] -A2- It is also syn. with fitonapN ; (T, S, M, K;) and, thus used, it is an inf. n., like maEoquwlN &c. (T, S, M.) See fitonapN , former half: and again, in the latter half. Hence, (T, M,) as some explain it, (M,) biA^ay~ikumu A@lomafotuwnu , [in the Kur lxviii. 6,] (T, M,) meaning In which of you is madness: (T:) but some say that the b is redundant; (M;) thus says AO; (T;) the meaning being A^ay~ukumu A@lomafotuwnu [ Which of you is the afflicted with madness ]; (T, M;) but Zj disallowed this: (T:) J says, [in the S,] that the b is redundant, as in kafaY biA@ll~`hi $ahiydFA , in the Kur [xiii. last verse, &c.], and [thus in copies of the S, app. a mistake for “ or ”] Almftwn means Alfitonapu , and is an inf. n. [&c.]: IB says, [in remarking upon this passage of the S,] if the b be redundant, Almftwn is the man, and is not an inf. n.; but if you make the b to be not redundant, then Almftwn is an inf. n. in the sense of Alfutuwn . (TA.) [See also art. b ; p. 142, second col.; and p. 143, third col.]
